definition_zh: 全职的；全日制的；占用全部时间的；以全职方式
definition_en: covering the whole of a normal working or study week rather than only part of it
core_image: 一整块时间被填得满满的，不留一点空档
scene: 她在诊所上完一整周的班，没有半天空闲。After years of part-time shifts, she finally signed a fulltime contract at the clinic.
sceneCN: 这里 fulltime 是「全职的」（第 1 个义项：占满整个正常工作周）；句意：做了多年兼职之后，她终于在诊所签下了一份全职合同。

pos.zh: 全职的；全日制的；占用全部时间的
以全职方式；全职地

derivatives.zh: 全职工作者；由 fulltime 加表人后缀 -er 构成
全职的；fulltime 的连字符标准拼写，语义不变

senses.title: A post that fills the whole week
senses.definition: describing a job or post that takes the whole of a normal working week
senses.definitionCN: 指占满整个正常工作周的职位或工作
senses.example: He gave up two part-time jobs for one fulltime post at the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 他放弃了两份兼职，换来了医院的一份全职职位。
senses.why: Full gives the idea of being filled up and time gives the week, so the compound names work that leaves no free hours.
senses.whyCN: full 提供「填满」的意思，time 提供「时间」，合成词因此指不留空闲工时的劳动。

senses.title: A course that fills the whole study week
senses.definition: describing study that occupies the whole of a normal academic week
senses.definitionCN: 指占满整个正常教学周的学习或课程
senses.example: She switched from evening classes to a fulltime design course.
senses.exampleCN: 她从夜校课程转到了全日制设计课程。
senses.why: The same completeness moves from paid work to study, where it stands against part-time arrangements.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「满」从带薪工作移到学习上，用来与「部分时间」的安排相对。

senses.title: Working the whole week
senses.definition: in a way that fills the whole working week
senses.definitionCN: 以占满整个工作周的方式
senses.example: After the baby was born, he went back to work fulltime.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子出生后，他重新回去做全职工作。
senses.why: As an adverb the word drops the noun and keeps only the measure of a whole week of commitment.
senses.whyCN: 作副词时省去了名词，只留下「整整一周都投入」这个度量。

senses.title: Taking all of the time available
senses.titleCN: 占用全部时间的；不分时段的
senses.definition: using or needing all of the time that is available, not just a part of it
senses.definitionCN: 占用或需要全部可用时间，而不只是一部分
senses.example: Caring for his father became a fulltime concern.
senses.exampleCN: 照顾父亲成了他全天候的操心事。
senses.why: Outside jobs and schools the word simply means that an activity fills all the time a person has.
senses.whyCN: 离开工作和学校语境后，这个词只表示某件事占满了一个人所有的时间。

senses.title: A guaranteed whole week contract
senses.titleCN: 全职性质的（合同或岗位）
senses.definition: describing a contract or position that guarantees the whole normal working week
senses.definitionCN: 指保证整个正常工作时长的合同或岗位
senses.example: The union is pressing the company for more fulltime contracts.
senses.exampleCN: 工会正敦促公司提供更多全职合同。
senses.why: In labour talk the adjective attaches to the contract itself, naming a guarantee of whole week hours rather than a single shift.
senses.whyCN: 在劳工语境里，这个词直接修饰合同，指对整周工时的保证，而不是某一天的班。

intro.en: Fulltime joins two Old English words, full and time, and the compound is first recorded in the nineteenth century, in sport before employment.
intro.cn: fulltime 由两个古英语词 full 与 time 复合而成，一般认为这个复合形式在十九世纪先出现于体育，再进入就业领域。

items.en: The reconstructed root pele means to fill, and full descends from it.
items.cn: 重构形式的原始印欧语词根 pele 意为「填满」，full 由它而来。

items.en: Full means filled up and tima means time or season.
items.cn: full 意为「装满的」，tima 意为「时间、时节」。

items.en: Full and time already appear together in phrases for a whole period.
items.cn: 中古英语里 full 与 time 已一起出现在表示「整段时期」的短语中。

items.en: Full time names the end of a match in football and other sports.
items.cn: full time 在足球等运动里指比赛终场。

items.en: Fulltime spreads to jobs and study as the opposite of part time.
items.cn: fulltime 扩展到工作与学习，成为 part time 的反面。

note.en: Fulltime is an English compound, so its neighbours are the two words that build it and the compounds made on the same pattern.
note.cn: fulltime 是英语复合词，因此与它相邻的是构成它的两个词，以及按同一模式造出的复合词。

entries.definition: holding as much as possible, with no space left
a person who works the whole of the normal week
hours worked beyond the normal working week
lasting for a long time without planned end
paid a fixed amount each month rather than by the hour
covering only part of the normal working week

normalIntro.en: Fulltime is best remembered as a filled timetable: every box of the working week is taken.
normalIntro.cn: fulltime 最好记成一张被填满的课表：工作周的每一格都被占上了。

normal.en: Full is the same word as in a full cup, so fulltime means a cup of time with nothing missing.
normal.cn: full 就是「满杯」里的 full，所以 fulltime 指一杯装满、什么都不缺的时间。

normal.en: Time is the word for hours, so the compound measures how many hours are filled.
normal.cn: time 指钟点，所以这个复合词衡量的是被填满了多少小时。

normal.en: A fulltime job stands opposite a part-time job.
normal.cn: fulltime job 与 part-time job 相对。

normal.en: Fulltime study means the whole study week, not a few evening classes.
normal.cn: fulltime study 指整周都在学习，而不是上几节夜课。

normal.en: The hyphenated form full-time is the same word, only written with a link.
normal.cn: 带连字符的 full-time 是同一个词，只是多了一道连接符。

abstract.en: See a timetable where every square is painted the same colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一张课表，每一格都被涂成同一种颜色。

abstract.en: See a reading room lit from morning to night, with books open all day.
abstract.cn: 想象一间从早亮到晚的阅览室，书整天摊开着。

abstract.en: See a worker with a badge, standing at the same post from the first shift to the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一个挂着工牌的工人，从第一班一直站到最后一班。

examples.en: She works fulltime at a small design studio.
examples.cn: 她在一家小设计工作室做全职工作。

examples.en: The college offers both fulltime and part-time courses.
examples.cn: 这所学院同时开设全日制和兼职课程。

examples.en: A fulltime job leaves little room for a second career.
examples.cn: 一份全职工作几乎不留余地给第二份事业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「full + time」——把「满」和「时间」拼在一起，就是全部时间都投入的全职；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: full（古英语 full，满的；源自原始日耳曼语 fullaz，可上溯到重构形式的原始印欧语词根 pele「填满」）+ time（古英语 tima，时间）→ fulltime，字面「时间被填满」，即全职。

sensesIntro.en: Fulltime starts from paid work that fills the whole week, then moves to full time study, to adverb use, to any activity that takes all available time, and finally to the contract that guarantees such hours.
sensesIntro.cn: fulltime 从占满整周的有薪工作出发，依次扩展到全日制学习、副词用法、占用全部时间的活动，最后指保证整周工时的合同。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole block of week time filled to the brim.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整块周时间被填得满满的。

branches.en: Paid work that fills the whole week is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 占满整周的有薪工作是日常义项。

branches.en: Study that fills the academic week is the school sense.
branches.cn: 占满教学周的学习是学校义项。

branches.en: The adverb keeps the measure of a whole week but drops the noun.
branches.cn: 副词用法保留整周的度量，但省去了名词。

branches.en: Any activity that takes all available time extends the image.
branches.cn: 任何占用全部可用时间的活动都是这一意象的延伸。

branches.en: A fulltime post and a fulltime contract both promise whole week hours.
branches.cn: 全职职位与全职合同都承诺整周的工时。

intro.en: Fulltime is an English compound of two free morphemes, full and time, and part time, overtime, and full-timer follow the same pattern.
intro.cn: fulltime 是由 full 与 time 两个自由语素构成的英语复合词，part time、overtime、full-timer 都按同一模式构成。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic, so the word has no Latin ancestor and no Latin cognate family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的两半都属日耳曼语源，没有拉丁语祖先，也没有拉丁同源词族，因此下面的同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Full marks the idea of being filled up.
items.exampleCN: full 表示「装满」的意思。

items.meaning: hours or a period available for an activity
items.example: Time supplies the measured week.
items.exampleCN: time 提供被计量的那一周。

items.example: Full-time is the hyphenated spelling.
items.exampleCN: full-time 是带连字符的拼写。

items.meaning: covering only part of the week
items.example: Part-time is the opposite compound.
items.exampleCN: part-time 是反义的复合词。

items.meaning: a person who works whole week hours
items.example: The suffix -er names the person.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 指做这件事的人。

items.meaningCN: 表示「做某事的人」的后缀
items.example: The suffix -er forms full-timer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 full-timer。

items.example: The element -time forms overtime and half-time.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -time 构成 overtime 与 half-time。

items.meaning: hours worked beyond the normal week
items.example: Overtime extends time beyond the full week.
items.exampleCN: overtime 把时间延长到整周之外。

items.meaning: half of a working day or half of a match
items.example: Half-time cuts the full period in two.
items.exampleCN: half-time 把整段时期切成两半。

items.example: Fullness keeps the adjective idea as a noun.
items.exampleCN: fullness 把形容词的意思保留为名词。

definition_zh: 摸索；笨拙地摸找；笨手笨脚地处理；搞砸
definition_en: to search for something or handle it clumsily with the hands
core_image: 黑灯里双手乱摸，钥匙在指间滑来滑去就是抓不住
scene: 厨房的灯坏了，他伸手在抽屉里摸来摸去找不到勺子。In the dark kitchen he fumbled for a spoon in the drawer.
sceneCN: 这里 fumble 是「摸索着找」（第 1 个义项：手忙脚乱地摸找）；句意：厨房的灯坏了，他在抽屉里摸来摸去找不到勺子。

pos.zh: 摸索；笨拙地摸找；笨手笨脚地处理；搞砸
摸索；笨拙的动作

derivatives.zh: 笨手笨脚的人；由 fumble 加表人后缀 -er 构成
摸索；笨拙的动作；由动词加 -ing 构成的名词
笨拙地；摸索地；由 fumbling 加副词后缀 -ly 构成

senses.title: Searching with the hands
senses.definition: to search for something by moving the hands about awkwardly, often because of darkness or nerves
senses.definitionCN: 因看不清或紧张而双手乱动地寻找某物
senses.example: She fumbled for the light switch along the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 她摸着墙壁找电灯开关。
senses.why: The verb pictures hands that cannot settle on an object, so the first sense is groping rather than holding.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词画的是双手始终落不到物体上的样子，所以第一个义项是摸找而不是握持。

senses.title: Handling something clumsily
senses.definition: to hold, move, or work something in a clumsy way, often nearly dropping it
senses.definitionCN: 笨拙地拿、移动或操作某物，常常差点把它弄掉
senses.example: He fumbled with the zip on his jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 他笨手笨脚地拉外套的拉链。
senses.why: Once the hands find the object the same awkwardness continues, so groping grows into clumsy handling.
senses.whyCN: 双手找到物体之后，那份笨拙并没有消失，于是「摸找」长成了「笨拙地操作」。

senses.title: Losing something by clumsy handling
senses.definition: to mishandle a chance, a task, or a message so that it is lost
senses.definitionCN: 把机会、任务或消息处理失当而失去它
senses.example: The clerk fumbled an easy question and lost the sale.
senses.exampleCN: 店员把一个小问题处理砸了，丢掉了这单生意。
senses.why: If clumsy hands can drop a cup, they can also drop an opportunity, which is the figurative extension.
senses.whyCN: 笨手能摔掉杯子，也就能摔掉机会，这就是比喻性的延伸。

senses.title: Dropping the ball in sport
senses.definition: in ball games, to drop the ball or lose control of it
senses.definitionCN: 在球类运动中没接住球或失去对球的控制
senses.example: The fullback fumbled the ball near his own line.
senses.exampleCN: 后卫在自家阵线附近漏接了球。
senses.why: Sport gives the clumsy hands a concrete object, so the general sense narrows to a dropped ball.
senses.whyCN: 体育给了笨拙的双手一个具体对象，一般含义于是收窄成「掉球」。

senses.title: Struggling for words
senses.definition: to speak with pauses and hesitation while searching for the right words
senses.definitionCN: 说话时停顿犹豫，边想边找合适的词
senses.example: He fumbled for a name and then gave up.
senses.exampleCN: 他结结巴巴地想找个名字，最后放弃了。
senses.why: Words are treated like small objects that the tongue tries to pick up, so speech borrows the hand image.
senses.whyCN: 词被当成舌头要去捡起的小物件，于是说话借用了手部的意象。

intro.en: The origin of fumble is uncertain; it is generally linked to Middle English fomelen, to grope, and to similar Low German and Norse words for awkward groping.
intro.cn: fumble 的来源不确定，一般认为与中古英语 fomelen（摸索）以及低地德语、北欧语中表示笨拙摸索的近形词有关。

items.en: Falma means to grope with the hands.
items.cn: falma 意为用手摸索。

items.en: Fomelen means to grope about and is the closest English ancestor.
items.cn: fomelen 意为到处摸索，是最接近的英语前身。

items.en: Fummeln means to fumble or paw at something.
items.cn: fummeln 意为乱摸、笨手笨脚地弄。

items.en: The verb is recorded in the sixteenth century with the sense of handling awkwardly.
items.cn: 一般认为这个动词在十六世纪以「笨拙地处理」的含义被记录。

items.en: Sport adds the dropped ball and everyday speech adds fumbling for words.
items.cn: 现代英语里，体育加上「掉球」义，日常口语加上「找词」义。

note.en: Fumble belongs to the word family of awkward hands, next to the nouns and adverbs built on it, and to verbs of groping and floundering.
note.cn: fumble 属于「手不听使唤」这一词族，与它构成的名称和副词相邻，也与表示摸索、慌乱的动词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who handles things in a clumsy way
the act of groping, or a hesitant manner
to trip while walking or to make a mistake
entries.definitionCN: 绊倒；出错（与 fumble 只是读音和拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to search blindly with the hands
to struggle helplessly without a clear direction
to deal with something badly

normalIntro.en: Fumble is a verb of the hands: the grip keeps slipping, whether on a key, a zip, a ball, or a name.
normalIntro.cn: fumble 是一个「手」的动词：抓住的东西总在滑走，可能是钥匙、拉链、球，也可能是一个名字。

normal.en: A fumble in sport is a dropped ball, and the verb keeps that picture of a lost grip.
normal.cn: fumble 在体育里指掉球，动词保留了「抓不住」的画面。

normal.en: Fumble for something means the hands search without finding it at once.
normal.cn: fumble for 表示双手摸索，不能立刻找到。

normal.en: Fumble with a zip or a key means you are handling it badly.
normal.cn: fumble with 表示把拉链或钥匙弄得笨手笨脚。

normal.en: The -ing form fumbling often describes a nervous, hesitant manner.
normal.cn: fumbling 这个形式常用来形容紧张犹豫的样子。

normal.en: Compare stumble: feet stumble, hands fumble.
normal.cn: 对比 stumble：脚会绊倒，手会乱摸。

abstract.en: See a hand sweeping an empty shelf in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在黑暗里扫过空空的架子。

abstract.en: See a button that will not pass through its hole, however the fingers twist.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗扣子怎么也穿不过扣眼，手指怎么拧都不行。

abstract.en: See a chance passing between two slow hands and falling.
abstract.cn: 想象一个机会从两只慢吞吞的手之间滑过，掉了下去。

examples.en: She fumbled in her bag for the ticket.
examples.cn: 她在包里摸索着找票。

examples.en: He fumbles with the buttons whenever he is nervous.
examples.cn: 他一紧张就会笨手笨脚地弄扣子。

examples.en: The team fumbled a clear chance in the last minute.
examples.cn: 球队在最后一分钟错失了一个明显的机会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fum」听上去像「翻」，「ble」像「不了」——翻来翻去也翻不出来，正是摸索；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定：一般认为 fumble 与中古英语 fomelen（摸索）、低地德语 fummeln（乱摸）、古诺尔斯语 falma（摸索）同源，核心是「双手落不到实处」，十六世纪起见于英语。

sensesIntro.en: Fumble begins with hands groping in the dark, passes to clumsy handling, to mishandling a chance, to dropping a ball, and ends with a tongue searching for words.
sensesIntro.cn: fumble 从黑暗中双手摸找开始，转到笨拙的操作，再到错失机会、漏接球，最后落到舌头上找词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands that cannot get a grip on the thing they want.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手怎么也抓不住想要的东西。

branches.en: Groping in the dark is the root sense of the verb.
branches.cn: 黑暗中摸索是这个动词的根本义。

branches.en: Clumsy handling keeps the same awkward hands on a found object.
branches.cn: 笨拙操作把同样笨拙的双手放到已经找到的物体上。

branches.en: A mishandled chance is a dropped object seen figuratively.
branches.cn: 被处理砸的机会，就是比喻意义上掉落的物体。

branches.en: Sport narrows the sense to a ball that leaves the hands.
branches.cn: 体育语境把词义收窄到离开双手的球。

branches.en: A lost chance and a lost word are both failures of grip.
branches.cn: 错失的机会与找不到的词，都是「抓不住」的失败。

intro.en: Fumble is a simple English verb with a small family: fumbler, fumbling, and fumblingly are built with -er, -ing, and -ly.
intro.cn: fumble 是一个简单的英语动词，词族不大：fumbler、fumbling、fumblingly 分别由 -er、-ing、-ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: The verb has no Latin ancestor; its origin is uncertain and the likely sources are Germanic, so the Latin cognate list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个动词没有拉丁语祖先，来源不确定，可能的来源都属日耳曼语，因此拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Fumble is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: fumble 是整个词族的基础。

items.meaningCN: 表示「做某事的人」的后缀
items.example: The suffix -er forms fumbler.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 fumbler。

items.example: Fumbler names the person who drops things.
items.exampleCN: fumbler 指总把东西弄掉的人。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms fumbling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 fumbling。

items.example: Fumbling keeps the action as a noun.
items.exampleCN: fumbling 把动作保留为名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示「以……方式」的副词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ly forms fumblingly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 fumblingly。

items.example: Fumblingly describes how the hand moves.
items.exampleCN: fumblingly 描述手部动作的方式。

items.meaningCN: 被笨拙处理过的；掉落的
items.example: Fumbled records the completed action.
items.exampleCN: fumbled 记录已完成的动作。

items.meaning: a clumsy drop, especially of a ball
items.meaningCN: 失手掉落（尤指球）；笨拙的动作
items.example: The noun fumble names the dropped ball.
items.exampleCN: 名词 fumble 指掉落的那个球。

items.meaning: third person singular, and the plural of the noun
items.meaningCN: 三单形式；名词的复数形式
items.example: Fumbles carries both grammatical roles.
items.exampleCN: fumbles 同时承担两种语法角色。

definition_zh: 功能；作用；职能；函数；典礼；运转
definition_en: the purpose or duty that something or someone is meant to carry out
core_image: 机器里每个零件各就各位，按自己的职责转动
scene: 这台旧收音机还能响，里面的零件都还在做原来的事。Every part of the old radio still has a function, even after many years.
sceneCN: 这里 function 是「功能；作用」（第 1 个义项：某物被设计来完成的事）；句意：这台旧收音机还能响，多年之后每个零件都还在发挥原来的作用。

senses.title: The purpose a thing is made for
senses.definition: the purpose or role that a thing is designed to perform
senses.definitionCN: 某物被设计来完成的目的或所起的作用
senses.example: The function of the brake is to stop the wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 刹车的作用是让车轮停下。
senses.why: Latin fungi means to perform, so the noun first names the job a thing performs.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fungi 意为履行，所以这个名词首先指某物所履行的职事。

senses.title: The duty of a person or office
senses.definition: the duties that belong to a person or to an official position
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个人或某个职位的职责
senses.example: The treasurer has a clear function in the club.
senses.exampleCN: 财务主管在俱乐部里有明确的职责。
senses.why: The word moves from tools to people, and the duty becomes the function of an office.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从工具移到人身上，职务上的责任就成了「职能」。

senses.title: To operate as a machine does
senses.definition: to operate or work properly, as a machine or a system does
senses.definitionCN: 像机器或系统那样正常地运转和工作
senses.example: The lift is still not functioning after the repair.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯修过之后仍然不能正常运转。
senses.why: A thing that performs its job is said to function, which turns the noun into a verb of working.
senses.whyCN: 一个能履行职事的东西就被说成 function，名词于是变成表示「运转」的动词。

senses.title: To serve in the place of something
senses.definition: to serve as something or to play the part of something else
senses.definitionCN: 充当某物，或起到另一物的作用
senses.example: The old school now functions as a community centre.
senses.exampleCN: 那所旧学校现在充当社区中心。
senses.why: When one thing takes over the role of another, it functions as that thing.
senses.whyCN: 当一物接替另一物的角色时，它就是在「充当」那一物。

senses.title: A rule in mathematics
senses.definition: in mathematics, a rule that assigns exactly one output to each input
senses.definitionCN: 数学中把每个输入对应到唯一输出的规则
senses.example: The graph shows how this function rises and falls.
senses.exampleCN: 这张图显示这个函数如何上升和下降。
senses.why: Latin functio named a performance, and mathematics borrows it for a rule that performs a mapping.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 functio 本指履行，数学借它来表示执行一种对应关系的规则。

senses.title: A formal gathering
senses.definition: a formal official or social gathering held for a set purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为特定目的举办的正式官方或社交聚会
senses.example: The hall was hired for a charity function.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅被租下来办一场慈善聚会。
senses.why: A function is also an occasion that has a set purpose, so the sense widens from duty to event.
senses.whyCN: function 也指有固定目的的场合，词义于是从「职责」扩展到「活动」。

intro.en: Function comes from Latin functio, a performance or discharge of duty, built on the verb fungi, to perform.
intro.cn: function 来自拉丁语 functio（履行、职务的执行），由动词 fungi（履行）构成。

items.en: Fungi means to perform or to discharge a duty.
items.cn: fungi 意为履行、完成职责。

items.en: Functio means a performance or the discharge of an office.
items.cn: functio 意为履行、职务的执行。

items.en: Fonction carries the noun into French with the sense of an office.
items.cn: fonction 把这个名词带入法语，意为职务。

items.en: Function first names an office or a duty in English.
items.cn: 一般认为 function 在十四世纪先指职务或职责。

items.en: Mathematics adds the algebraic function, and social life adds the formal event.
items.cn: 现代英语里，数学加上代数的「函数」义，社交生活加上「典礼」义。

note.en: Function sits at the centre of a Latin family, with functional, functionality, and functionary around it, and near role, purpose, and duty.
note.cn: function 位于一个拉丁词族的中心，周围有 functional、functionality、functionary，近处则是 role、purpose、duty。

normalIntro.en: Function is a Latin word for performing a duty, so every sense keeps the idea of a part busy at its own job.
normalIntro.cn: function 是拉丁语里「履行职责」的词，因此每个义项都保留「一个部件忙着做自己的事」的意思。

normal.en: Function and functionary share the Latin base fungi, to perform.
normal.cn: function 与 functionary 共享拉丁语词基 fungi（履行）。

normal.en: A function is what a part is for, as a key is for opening a lock.
normal.cn: function 就是一个部件的用处，就像钥匙是用来开锁的。

normal.en: Function as means to act in the place of something else.
normal.cn: function as 表示代替另一物起作用。

normal.en: A mathematical function keeps the idea of a rule that performs a mapping.
normal.cn: 数学里的 function 保留了「执行一种对应关系」的意思。

normal.en: Compare role: a role belongs to a person, a function belongs to a part or an office.
normal.cn: 对比 role：role 多属于人，function 多属于部件或职位。

abstract.en: See a machine where every part is busy at its own task.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器，每个零件都在忙自己的那份活。

abstract.en: See a name plate on an office door; whoever sits there takes on the duty.
abstract.cn: 想象办公室门上的名牌，谁坐在那里就担起那份职责。

abstract.en: See gears biting and turning with a steady hum.
abstract.cn: 想象齿轮咬合着转动，发出稳定的低鸣。

examples.en: The heart functions as a pump for the whole body.
examples.cn: 心脏为全身起着泵的作用。

examples.en: The old radio still functions well after the repair.
examples.cn: 这台旧收音机修好之后仍然运转良好。

examples.en: A social function brought the whole village together.
examples.cn: 一场社交聚会把整个村子聚到了一起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「funct」像「放克」的节拍——每个部件都踩着自己的拍子干活，这就是功能；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fungi（履行、执行）→ 名词 functio（履行；职责）→ 古法语 fonction → 英语 function，核心义「按职责运转」。

sensesIntro.en: Function runs from the purpose of a part, to the duty of an office, to the working of a machine, to serving as something else, to a mathematical rule, and finally to a formal event.
sensesIntro.cn: function 从部件的作用，到职位的职能，到机器的运转，再到充当另一物、数学上的函数，最后到正式的聚会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every part of a machine busy at its own assigned task.
core.cn: 核心意象：机器里每个零件都在忙自己被分派的那份活。

branches.en: The purpose of a part is the first and most common sense.
branches.cn: 部件的作用是最早也最常见的义项。

branches.en: The duty of a person or an office carries the same idea to people.
branches.cn: 人或职位的职责把同一个意思移到人身上。

branches.en: Working properly is the verb sense that grows from the noun.
branches.cn: 正常运转是由名词长出的动词义。

branches.en: A mathematical rule performs a mapping, so it borrows the name.
branches.cn: 数学规则执行一种对应，因此借用了这个名字。

branches.en: A duty and a formal event are both occasions with a set purpose.
branches.cn: 职责与正式聚会都是有固定目的的场合。

intro.en: Function carries a Latin core and an English family built with -al, -ality, -ary, and -ing.
intro.cn: function 带着一个拉丁语核心，以及由 -al、-ality、-ary、-ing 构成的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin fungi means to perform, functio means a performance, and functus is the participle for having performed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fungi 意为履行，functio 意为履行之事，functus 是表示「已履行」的分词。

definition_en: concerned with the way something works or is used rather than with how it looks
core_image: 只看零件转不转、好不好用，不管外壳好不好看
scene: 这把椅子样子普通，坐上去却稳当又好用。The plain chair is not beautiful, but it is functional and comfortable.
sceneCN: 这里 functional 是「实用的」（第 2 个义项：以实用为主而非好看）；句意：这把椅子样子普通，但坐上去稳当又实用。

功能语言（用于交际的语言）

senses.title: Relating to function
senses.definition: relating to the way something works or is used rather than to its appearance
senses.definitionCN: 与某物的运作或使用方式有关，而不是与外观有关
senses.example: The report looks at the functional side of the design.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告关注设计的功能层面。
senses.why: The suffix -al turns function into an adjective of relation, so functional first means belonging to function.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把 function 变成表关系的形容词，因此 functional 首先指「属于功能的」。

senses.title: Useful rather than decorative
senses.definition: designed to be useful and efficient rather than to look attractive
senses.definitionCN: 以好用、高效为目的，而不是为了好看
senses.example: The furniture is plain but strictly functional.
senses.exampleCN: 这件家具朴素，但完全以实用为主。
senses.why: Once the adjective judges things by their use, plain and useful becomes a virtue instead of a fault.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词以用途来评判事物时，朴素好用就从缺点变成了优点。

senses.title: Working properly
senses.titleCN: 能正常工作的；功能完好的
senses.definition: working, or able to work, in the normal way
senses.definitionCN: 能按正常方式工作或运转的
senses.example: The website is fully functional again after the update.
senses.exampleCN: 更新之后网站又能正常使用了。
senses.why: A thing that does its job is functional, so the adjective also reports that a system is in working order.
senses.whyCN: 能完成本职的东西就是 functional，因此这个形容词也用来表示系统处于可用状态。

senses.title: A technical approach to use
senses.definition: in linguistics and mathematics, describing a method that studies use, relations, or outputs rather than form alone
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学和数学中，指研究用途、关系或输出而不只看形式的方法
senses.example: Functional grammar asks what a sentence is doing in a conversation.
senses.exampleCN: 功能语法追问一句话在对话里起什么作用。
senses.why: Technical fields borrow the adjective when the working of a system, not its shape, is the object of study.
senses.whyCN: 技术领域研究的是系统如何运作而不是它的外形，于是借用了这个形容词。

senses.title: Of an illness without visible damage
senses.definition: of an illness, having no clear damage in the structure of an organ although its working is disturbed
senses.definitionCN: 指器官结构没有明显损伤、但功能受到扰乱的疾病
senses.example: The doctor called it a functional disorder, with no damage to the stomach itself.
senses.exampleCN: 医生称之为功能性疾病，胃本身没有损伤。
senses.why: Medicine separates the structure of an organ from its working, so a fault in working alone is called functional.
senses.whyCN: 医学把器官的结构与运作分开，只出在运作上的毛病就被称为 functional。

intro.en: Functional is an English adjective built on function with the Latin suffix -alis, which marks a relation.
intro.cn: functional 是在 function 上加拉丁语后缀 -alis（表关系）构成的英语形容词。

items.en: Functio means a performance or the discharge of a duty.
items.cn: functio 意为履行、职务的执行。

items.en: The suffix -alis forms adjectives that mean relating to.
items.cn: 后缀 -alis 构成表示「与……有关的」形容词。

items.en: Fonction carries the noun into French before it reaches English.
items.cn: fonction 先把这个词带入法语，再进入英语。

items.en: Functional is recorded in the seventeenth century, built on function with the Latin suffix.
items.cn: 一般认为 functional 在十七世纪出现，由 function 加拉丁语后缀构成。

items.en: Modern use spreads the adjective to design, medicine, and linguistics.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个形容词扩展到设计、医学和语言学。

note.en: Functional is the adjective of function, so its look-alikes are the noun and the derived noun and adverb, and its near meanings are words for usefulness.
note.cn: functional 是 function 的形容词，形近的是那个名词以及由它派生的名词和副词，近义的则是表示「有用」的词。

normalIntro.en: Functional is function with an adjective ending, so it always asks what a thing does rather than how it looks.
normalIntro.cn: functional 就是加了形容词词尾的 function，所以它总是问「这东西做什么用」，而不是「它好不好看」。

normal.en: Function plus -al gives an adjective about use, not about looks.
normal.cn: function 加上 -al，得到的是讲用途而不是讲外观的形容词。

normal.en: Fully functional means every part works as it should.
normal.cn: fully functional 表示每个部件都在正常工作。

normal.en: Functional design puts use before ornament.
normal.cn: functional design 把用途放在装饰之前。

normal.en: A functional disorder is one where the organ looks fine but works badly.
normal.cn: functional disorder 指器官看起来完好、运作却出了问题。

normal.en: Compare practical: practical stresses usefulness in practice, functional stresses the working part.
normal.cn: 对比 practical：practical 强调实际好用，functional 强调运作的那一面。

abstract.en: See a machine opened up, with every part labelled by what it does.
abstract.cn: 想象一台被拆开的机器，每个零件都标着它负责做什么。

abstract.en: See a plain wooden stool with no carving, used every day.
abstract.cn: 想象一张没有雕花的朴素木凳，天天都在用。

abstract.en: See a green light on a panel, showing that the system is running.
abstract.cn: 想象面板上亮起一盏绿灯，表示系统正在运行。

examples.en: The kitchen is small but highly functional.
examples.cn: 这间厨房不大，但非常实用。

examples.en: The website is fully functional again after the update.
examples.cn: 更新之后网站又能完全正常使用了。

examples.en: Functional design puts use before ornament.
examples.cn: 功能设计把用途放在装饰之前。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「function + al」——给「功能」加上一条形容尾巴，就成了「功能的、实用的」；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 functio（履行；职责）+ 形容词后缀 -alis（与……有关的）→ 英语 function 加 -al → functional，核心义「与运作方式有关的」。

sensesIntro.en: Functional begins as the adjective of function, then judges things as useful, reports that a system works, names a technical method, and finally describes an illness of working rather than structure.
sensesIntro.cn: functional 起初只是 function 的形容词，继而评判事物是否实用、说明系统能否运转，再指一种技术方法，最后描述只有运作出问题、结构无损的疾病。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: only the working parts count, never the shell around them.
core.cn: 核心意象：只看里面能不能转，不看外面好不好看。

branches.en: The plain adjective of relation is the first sense.
branches.cn: 最朴素的表关系形容词义是第一项。

branches.en: Judging by use turns the adjective into praise for the practical.
branches.cn: 以用途作评判，使这个形容词变成对实用的赞许。

branches.en: A working system earns the adjective in everyday speech.
branches.cn: 在日常说法里，能运转的系统就配得上这个形容词。

branches.en: Linguistics and mathematics make the adjective a name for a method.
branches.cn: 语言学与数学把这个形容词变成一种方法的名称。

branches.en: A working system and a working organ share the same test of function.
branches.cn: 运转的系统与运作的器官，用的是同一把功能尺子。

senses.title: Forming the base of something
senses.definition: forming the base on which something is built or rests
senses.definitionCN: 构成某物赖以建立或承托的基础
senses.example: The fundamental layer of the road is gravel and stone.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路的基础层是碎石和石头。
senses.why: Latin fundus means the bottom, so the adjective names what sits lowest and carries the rest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fundus 意为底部，因此这个形容词指位于最下层、承托其余部分的东西。

senses.title: Essential and most important
senses.definition: more important than anything else because everything else depends on it
senses.definitionCN: 比任何别的东西都重要，因为其余一切都依赖它
senses.example: Trust is fundamental to any long partnership.
senses.exampleCN: 信任对任何长期合作都是根本的。
senses.why: A foundation is not only low but necessary, so the adjective grows into the sense of essential.
senses.whyCN: 地基不仅在最下面，而且必不可少，形容词于是长成「至关重要」的意思。

senses.title: The basic rules of a subject
senses.titleCN: 基本原理；基础（常用复数）
senses.definition: the basic facts or rules of a subject, usually used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 一门学科的基本事实或规则，通常用复数
senses.example: The first term covers the fundamentals of chemistry.
senses.exampleCN: 第一学期讲化学的基础原理。
senses.why: The noun keeps the physical image: the fundamentals are the ground under the rest of a subject.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了具体的意象：基础知识就是一门学科其余部分下面的那层地面。

senses.title: The lowest level in physics or music
senses.definition: in physics and music, describing the lowest or base level of a vibration or a system
senses.definitionCN: 在物理学和音乐中，指振动或系统的最低基础层次
senses.example: The fundamental frequency of the string sets its pitch.
senses.exampleCN: 弦的基频决定它的音高。
senses.why: Technical use takes the lowest layer literally: the fundamental tone or particle is the one the others are built on.
senses.whyCN: 技术用法把「最底层」照字面理解：基音或基本粒子就是其余部分赖以构成的那一层。

senses.title: The elementary level of study
senses.titleCN: 基础性的（教学或技能层面）
senses.definition: belonging to the first, elementary level of study or skill rather than an advanced one
senses.definitionCN: 属于学习或技能的最初、基础层面，而不是高级层面
senses.example: The school stresses fundamental skills such as reading and counting.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校强调阅读与算术等基础技能。
senses.why: Schools name the earliest level of a subject fundamental because all later work stands on it.
senses.whyCN: 学校把学科最初的那一层称为 fundamental，因为后面的学习都站在它上面。

intro.en: Fundamental comes from Latin fundamentum, a foundation, built on fundus, the bottom, with the relational suffix -alis.
intro.cn: fundamental 来自拉丁语 fundamentum（地基），由表示「底部」的 fundus 加表关系的后缀 -alis 构成。

items.en: Fundus means the bottom or the base of a thing.
items.cn: fundus 意为底部或某物的基底。

items.en: Fundare means to lay a base or to found something.
items.cn: fundare 意为打基础、奠定某物。

items.en: Fundamentum means a foundation, and with -alis it yields the adjective.
items.cn: fundamentum 意为地基，加上 -alis 便得出形容词。

items.en: Fundamental is recorded in English as an adjective meaning serving as a foundation.
items.cn: 一般认为 fundamental 在十六世纪以「作为基础的」这一形容词义进入英语。

items.en: Modern use adds the plural noun for the basics and the technical senses of physics and music.
items.cn: 现代用法加上表示基础知识的复数名词，以及物理和音乐中的技术义。

note.en: Fundamental is the adjective of the Latin word for a foundation, so its look-alikes are its own family and its near meanings are words for the basic and the essential.
note.cn: fundamental 是拉丁语「地基」一词的形容词，因此形近的是它自己的词族，近义的则是表示「基础」与「要紧」的词。

entries.definition: a base or foundation
in the most basic way
a strict movement that defends basic doctrines
simple and necessary, at the first level
absolutely necessary
lying beneath and causing what is visible

normalIntro.en: Fundamental is a foundation in adjective form, and the English word fund hides the same Latin bottom.
normalIntro.cn: fundamental 就是「地基」的形容词形式，而英语里的 fund 藏着同一个拉丁语「底部」。

normal.en: Fund, as in a bank fund, comes from the same Latin fundus, a bottom, so a fund is money placed at the base.
normal.cn: 银行里的 fund 与 fundamental 同出拉丁语 fundus（底部），所以 fund 是放在底下的那笔钱。

normal.en: Fundamental and fundament share the base fundus, bottom.
normal.cn: fundamental 与 fundament 共享词基 fundus（底部）。

normal.en: Fundamental to means at the base of something.
normal.cn: fundamental to 表示在某物的根基处。

normal.en: The fundamentals of a subject are the ground under its later chapters.
normal.cn: 一门学科的 fundamentals 就是后面各章下面的那层地面。

normal.en: Compare basic: basic is the everyday word, fundamental is stronger and more formal.
normal.cn: 对比 basic：basic 是日常词，fundamental 语气更强、更正式。

abstract.en: See a building with its foundation laid before any wall rises.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋楼先浇好地基，墙还没有砌起来。

abstract.en: See a rope bridge whose every plank depends on one thick post.
abstract.cn: 想象一座绳索桥，所有木板都系在一根粗柱子上。

abstract.en: See the first pages of a textbook, where all the simple rules are listed.
abstract.cn: 想象教科书最前面的几页，把最简单的规则都列在上面。

examples.en: Freedom of speech is a fundamental right.
examples.cn: 言论自由是一项基本权利。

examples.en: There is a fundamental difference between the two plans.
examples.cn: 这两个方案之间有根本性的差异。

examples.en: The course teaches the fundamentals of economics.
examples.cn: 这门课讲授经济学的基础原理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fund（底部）+ a + mental（精神的）」——精神底下那一层，就是根本；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fundus（底部、地基）→ fundare（打基础）→ fundamentum（地基）→ 一般认为晚期拉丁语由 fundamentum 加 -alis 构成形容词 → 英语 fundamental，核心义「在最底下承重的」。

sensesIntro.en: Fundamental starts as the adjective of a foundation, then means essential, then names the basics of a subject, and finally serves physics and music for the lowest level and schools for the first level of skill.
sensesIntro.cn: fundamental 起初是「地基」的形容词，继而表示至关重要，再指一门学科的基础知识，最后在物理和音乐中指最低层次，在学校语境中指最初级的技能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the lowest layer of a building, carrying every wall above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：建筑最底下那一层，承托上面的每一堵墙。

branches.en: The physical base is the literal first sense.
branches.cn: 具体的地基是最早的字面义项。

branches.en: Necessity turns the base into the essential.
branches.cn: 必不可少这一层意思，把「底部」变成了「至关重要」。

branches.en: The basics of a subject are the ground under later study.
branches.cn: 学科的基础知识就是后续学习下面的地面。

branches.en: Physics and music use the lowest level in a literal technical way.
branches.cn: 物理与音乐以技术方式直接使用「最低层次」。

branches.en: The basics and the elementary level are the same ground seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 基础原理与初级水平，是同一层地面从两侧看到的样子。

intro.en: Fundamental rests on the Latin base fundus, bottom, and grows an English family with -al, -ly, -ism, and -ist.
intro.cn: fundamental 立足于拉丁语词基 fundus（底部），并由 -al、-ly、-ism、-ist 长出一个英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin fundus means the bottom, fundare means to found, and fundamentum means a foundation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fundus 意为底部，fundare 意为奠定，fundamentum 意为地基。

items.meaning: the bottom or base of a thing
items.example: Fundus supplies the bottom image.
items.exampleCN: fundus 提供「底部」的意象。

items.meaning: to lay a base, to found
items.example: Fundare is the verb behind the family.
items.exampleCN: fundare 是这个词族背后的动词。

items.example: Fundamentum is the direct source of fundament.
items.exampleCN: fundamentum 是 fundament 的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -alis turns a noun of base into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -alis 把表示基础的名词变成形容词。

items.example: Fundamental is the head of the English family.
items.exampleCN: fundamental 是英语词族的核心。

items.example: Fundament keeps the Latin noun without the suffix.
items.exampleCN: fundament 保留了不带后缀的拉丁名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示「以……方式」的副词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ly forms fundamentally.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 fundamentally。

items.example: Fundamentally judges a matter at its base.
items.exampleCN: fundamentally 从根基上评判一件事。

items.meaning: a system of belief or practice
items.meaningCN: 表示学说或做法的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ism forms fundamentalism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 fundamentalism。

items.meaning: a strict defence of basic doctrines
items.example: Fundamentalism insists on the basics.
items.exampleCN: fundamentalism 坚持那些基础教义。

items.meaningCN: 表示追随者的表人后缀
items.example: The suffix -ist forms fundamentalist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 fundamentalist。

items.meaning: a person who defends basic doctrines strictly
items.example: Fundamentalist names the person.
items.exampleCN: fundamentalist 指这样的人。

definition_zh: 缆索铁路；缆车；索状的
definition_en: a railway on a steep slope that is worked by a cable, or something relating to a rope
core_image: 一根绷紧的钢缆把车厢沿陡坡一上一下地拽动
scene: 山城的老式缆车沿着陡坡缓缓上升。The old funicular climbs the steep hill slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 funicular 是「缆索铁路」（第 1 个义项：靠钢缆在陡坡上运行的铁路）；句意：山城的老式缆车沿着陡坡缓缓上升。

pos.zh: 缆索铁路；缆车
绳索的；索状的

derivatives.zh: 拉丁语指小形式，解剖学指神经或血管的索状束
植物学用语，指连接胚珠与子房的短柄
funiculus 加炎症后缀 -itis，指精索炎

senses.title: A railway worked by a cable
senses.definition: a railway that hauls cars up and down a steep slope with a moving cable
senses.definitionCN: 用运行中的钢缆把车厢拉上拉下陡坡的铁路
senses.example: The funicular connects the harbour with the old town on the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 这条缆索铁路把港口与崖上的老城连接起来。
senses.why: Latin funiculus means a small cord, and the whole railway is driven by one rope.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 funiculus 意为「细绳」，整条铁路正是由一根绳索驱动，所以这个词先指绳索，再指绳索铁路。

senses.title: A car of a cable railway
senses.definition: one of the passenger cars that runs on a funicular line
senses.definitionCN: 在缆索铁路上运行的载客车厢
senses.example: We waited for the second funicular to come down.
senses.exampleCN: 我们等第二辆缆车下山。
senses.why: The noun moved from the line itself to the vehicle that hangs on the cable.
senses.whyCN: 名词从「线路」转到「挂在钢缆上的车厢」，这是转喻式的扩展。

senses.title: Of or like a rope
senses.definition: relating to a rope or cord, or shaped like one
senses.definitionCN: 与绳索有关，或形状像绳索的
senses.example: The tendon runs in a funicular band along the wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 这条肌腱沿手腕形成一条索状带。
senses.why: The adjective is the oldest English use, taken straight from the Latin cord sense.
senses.whyCN: 形容词是英语中最早的用法，直接取自拉丁语「细绳」的词义。

senses.title: Of a cord-like nerve bundle
senses.definition: relating to a funiculus, a bundle of nerve fibres or vessels
senses.definitionCN: 与索状束（神经纤维或血管的束）有关的
senses.example: The surgeon examined the funicular part of the spermatic cord.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生检查了精索的索状部分。
senses.why: Medical Latin kept funiculus for any cord-like bundle, and the adjective followed it.
senses.whyCN: 医学拉丁语用 funiculus 指任何索状束，形容词随之进入解剖学。

senses.title: Of the stalk of an ovule
senses.definition: relating to the funicle, the short stalk that joins an ovule to the ovary
senses.definitionCN: 与珠柄（连接胚珠与子房的短柄）有关的
senses.example: The funicular stalk bends as the seed grows.
senses.exampleCN: 随着种子长大，珠柄弯了下来。
senses.why: Botany borrowed the same cord image for the short stalk of a seed.
senses.whyCN: 植物学借用了同一个「细绳」意象，指种子胚珠的那根短柄。

senses.title: Of a polygon of balanced forces
senses.definition: describing a polygon whose sides represent the lines of action of forces in balance
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种多边形，其各边代表处于平衡的各力的作用线
senses.example: The class drew a funicular polygon to test the roof load.
senses.exampleCN: 课堂上画了一个索多边形来检验屋顶荷载。
senses.why: In graphic statics each pull becomes a side of a closed figure, a rope turned into geometry.
senses.whyCN: 在图解静力学里，每一股拉力变成闭合图形的一条边，绳索由此变成几何。

intro.en: Funicular comes from Latin funiculus, a small cord, a diminutive of funis, rope.
intro.cn: funicular 来自拉丁语 funiculus（细绳），是 funis（绳索）的指小形式。

items.en: Funis means a rope or cord.
items.cn: funis 意为绳索或粗绳。

items.en: Funiculus is the diminutive, a small cord.
items.cn: funiculus 是指小形式，意为细绳。

items.en: The adjective first describes anything of a rope.
items.cn: 这个形容词最早描述与绳索有关之物。

items.en: Funicular railway names a line pulled by a cable.
items.cn: funicular railway 指靠钢缆牵引的铁路。

items.en: The word spreads to cliff lifts and city transit.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到崖壁缆车与城市交通。

note.en: Funicular sits in a small rope family and next to other cable-hauled mountain transport.
note.cn: funicular 属于一个小型的「绳索」词族，并与其它缆索山地交通工具相邻。

entries.definition: a small cord or a cord-like bundle
the stalk that attaches an ovule
inflammation of the spermatic cord
a vehicle pulled or suspended by a moving cable
entries.definitionCN: 由运行钢缆牵引或悬挂的车厢

entries.definition: a mountain railway that uses a toothed rack
a seat carried on a loop of cable
entries.definitionCN: 挂在循环钢缆上的座椅

normalIntro.en: Funicular hides the Latin word for a rope and the small-cord suffix that goes with it.
normalIntro.cn: funicular 里藏着拉丁语的「绳索」以及表示「细绳」的指小后缀。

normal.en: Funicular contains funis, the Latin word for a rope.
normal.cn: funicular 含有拉丁语 funis，意为绳索。

normal.en: The family runs funis, funiculus, funicle, funicular: every member is a cord.
normal.cn: 词族 funis、funiculus、funicle、funicular 都围绕绳索。

normal.en: A funicular railway is the full term, while funicular alone can name the line or the car.
normal.cn: funicular railway 是完整说法，单说 funicular 可以指线路或车厢。

normal.en: Compare cable car: a cable car may hang in the air, but a funicular keeps its wheels on rails.
normal.cn: 对比 cable car：缆车可以悬在空中，而 funicular 的车轮始终在轨道上。

normal.en: Fix the phrase ride the funicular for a steep climb in a city.
normal.cn: 记住搭配 ride the funicular，指乘坐缆车爬上陡坡。

abstract.en: Picture a taut steel cable on a slope, pulling a small car upward.
abstract.cn: 想象陡坡上一根绷紧的钢缆，正把小车厢往上拉。

abstract.en: Picture two cars meeting at the middle loop and passing each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两节车厢在中段会车、擦身而过。

abstract.en: Picture a thin cord under a lens, round and rope-like.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜下的一根细绳，圆而像索。

examples.en: The funicular takes visitors up the cliff in under three minutes.
examples.cn: 缆车不到三分钟就把游客送上崖顶。

examples.en: Engineers restored the old funicular rather than building a road.
examples.cn: 工程师修复了老缆车，而没有另修一条路。

examples.en: From the funicular station a path leads to the lighthouse.
examples.cn: 从缆车站有一条小路通往灯塔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扶你靠缆」——读音近似「扶你上缆车」，缆车正是把你扶上陡坡的绳索装置；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 funis（绳索）加指小后缀 -culus 构成 funiculus（细绳），再进入英语为 funicular，核心义是「用绳索牵引的」。

sensesIntro.en: Funicular starts as a word for a rope, becomes a steep cable railway and its car, then extends to cord-shaped things in anatomy, botany, and statics.
sensesIntro.cn: funicular 从「绳索」出发，转为陡坡上的缆索铁路与缆车车厢，再扩展到解剖学、植物学与静力学中的索状事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope that pulls a car up a slope.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根把车厢拉上陡坡的绳索。

branches.en: The cable railway is the concrete core sense.
branches.cn: 缆索铁路是具体的核心义项。

branches.en: The car is the vehicle branch of the same line.
branches.cn: 车厢是同一条线路上的载具分支。

branches.en: Rope shape and cord-like bundles share one image.
branches.cn: 绳索形状与索状束共享同一个意象。

branches.en: Line and car together form one transport system.
branches.cn: 线路与车厢合起来构成一套交通系统。

branches.en: The plant stalk and the force polygon are technical extensions of the cord.
branches.cn: 植物珠柄与力多边形是绳索意象的技术性延伸。

intro.en: Funicular is built from the Latin rope word funis, its diminutive funiculus, and an English adjective ending.
intro.cn: funicular 由拉丁语绳索词 funis、其指小形式 funiculus 以及英语形容词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin funis means a rope, and funiculus means a small cord; both feed the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 funis 意为绳索，funiculus 意为细绳，二者共同滋养了英语词族。

items.example: Funis is the plain Latin word for a rope.
items.exampleCN: funis 是拉丁语中表示绳索的常通用词。

items.example: Funiculus is a diminutive of funis.
items.exampleCN: funiculus 是 funis 的指小形式。

items.example: The suffix -culus makes a word mean little.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -culus 使词带有「小」的意思。

items.example: Funicle is the botanist short form.
items.exampleCN: funicle 是植物学中的简写形式。

items.example: Anatomy keeps funiculus for cord-like bundles.
items.exampleCN: 解剖学沿用 funiculus 指索状结构。

items.example: The adjective first described anything ropelike.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词最早描述绳索状之物。

items.example: The noun names the cable-worked railway.
items.exampleCN: 名词义指靠钢缆运行的铁路。

items.example: The compound fixes the transport sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词固定了交通义。

items.meaning: a cabin on a cable line
items.example: A funicular car hangs on the cable.
items.exampleCN: 缆车车厢悬挂在钢缆上。

definition_zh: 擦亮；翻新；使恢复光泽
definition_en: to polish something, or to restore it to a fresh condition
core_image: 一块旧银器被反复擦拭，重新亮了起来
scene: 阁楼里翻出的银烛台被擦得发亮。The old candlestick from the attic was furbished until it shone.
sceneCN: 这里 furbish 是「擦亮」（第 1 个义项：把表面擦到有光泽）；句意：阁楼里翻出的银烛台被擦得发亮。

pos.zh: 擦亮；翻新；使恢复光泽

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -er 构成，指擦亮或翻新的人
动词加 -ment 构成，指擦亮或翻新的过程
前缀 re- 加 furbish，指重新翻新、整修
re- 加 furbishment，指翻新工程

senses.title: To polish a surface
senses.definition: to rub a surface until it is clean and bright
senses.definitionCN: 把表面擦到干净而有光泽
senses.example: He furbished the brass plate with a soft cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 他用软布把铜牌擦得发亮。
senses.why: Old French forbir meant to polish, so physical shine is the oldest and plainest sense.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 forbir 本义就是擦亮，所以「把表面擦到发光」是最古老也最朴素的义项。

senses.title: To restore an old object
senses.definition: to clean and repair something old so that it looks fresh again
senses.definitionCN: 把旧物清洁修整，使它重新显得崭新
senses.example: They furbished the antique mirror before selling it.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在出售前把那面古董镜子翻新了一遍。
senses.why: Polishing an old thing grew into restoring it, because a shine makes age look fresh.
senses.whyCN: 擦拭旧物自然延伸为修复旧物，因为光泽会让岁月痕迹显得新鲜。

senses.title: To refresh knowledge or a skill
senses.definition: to brighten up knowledge or a skill that has grown dull through disuse
senses.definitionCN: 把因久未使用而变得生疏的知识或技能重新磨亮
senses.example: She furbished her French before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前她把自己的法语重新温习了一遍。
senses.why: The shine image moves from metal to the mind, where practice is the polishing cloth.
senses.whyCN: 「擦亮」的意象从金属转到头脑，练习就是那块抛光布。

senses.title: To smarten or embellish
senses.definition: to add touches that make something more attractive or impressive
senses.definitionCN: 添加点缀，使某物更悦目或更体面
senses.example: The essay was furbished with a few elegant quotations.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章用几句典雅引文作了修饰。
senses.why: Embellishment is polishing in a literary key: the surface is improved rather than repaired.
senses.whyCN: 修饰是「擦亮」的文学化说法：只改善表面，而不做真正的修复。

senses.title: To cleanse or purge, in older use
senses.definition: to cleanse something thoroughly, or to drive out what spoils it, in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中指彻底清洗，或驱除败坏之物
senses.example: The old rite was meant to furbish the house of sickness.
senses.exampleCN: 那套古老仪式意在把病气从屋里清除出去。
senses.why: Old French forbir also meant to clean out, a sense English kept only in archaic and ceremonial use.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 forbir 也有「清空、清除」之义，英语只在古旧与仪式性语境中保留了这个义项。

senses.title: To give a deceptive gloss
senses.definition: to give something a fresh surface that hides its real state
senses.definitionCN: 给某物一层新鲜表面，以掩盖其真实状况
senses.example: The accounts were furbished to look healthier than they were.
senses.exampleCN: 账目被粉饰得比实际更健康。
senses.why: A shine can sit only on the surface, so polishing turns into cosmetic cover-up.
senses.whyCN: 光泽可以只停留在表面，于是「擦亮」就滑向「粉饰门面」。

intro.en: Furbish comes from Old French forbir, to polish or clean, which is generally traced to a reconstructed Frankish verb.
intro.cn: furbish 来自古法语 forbir（擦亮、清洁），一般认为可追溯到重构的法兰克语动词。

items.en: A reconstructed verb, furbjan, means to clean or polish.
items.cn: 重构形式 furbjan，意为清洗或擦亮。

items.en: Forbir means to polish, clean, or purge.
items.cn: forbir 意为擦亮、清洁或清除。

items.en: English borrows furbish in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 furbish。

items.en: Writers extend it to refreshing and embellishing.
items.cn: 作家把它扩展到「刷新」与「修饰」。

items.en: Refurbish and furbishment keep the polish image alive.
items.cn: refurbish 与 furbishment 让「擦亮」的意象延续下来。

note.en: Furbish sits in a small native French family and next to the common polish words of English.
note.cn: furbish 属于一个来自法语的词族，并与英语中常见的「抛光」类词相邻。

entries.definition: to renovate or brighten again
a person who polishes something
the act of polishing or restoring
to rub a surface until it shines
to make metal shine by rubbing
to restore an old building or room

normalIntro.en: Furbish is a polishing verb that comes through French, and its family grows with a prefix and two suffixes.
normalIntro.cn: furbish 是经由法语进入英语的「擦亮」动词，其词族靠一个前缀和两个后缀扩展。

normal.en: Old French forbir meant to polish and clean, and English kept the shine.
normal.cn: 古法语 forbir 意为擦亮与清洁，英语保留了「光泽」这层意思。

normal.en: Furbish and refurbish differ by one prefix: re- adds the idea of doing it again.
normal.cn: furbish 与 refurbish 只差一个前缀：re- 表示「再做一次」。

normal.en: Furbish up is the phrasal form, meaning to renovate or refresh.
normal.cn: furbish up 是短语形式，意为翻新或刷新。

normal.en: The family includes furbisher and furbishment, both built directly on the verb.
normal.cn: 词族包括 furbisher 与 furbishment，二者都直接由动词构成。

normal.en: Furbish often takes an old object: a sword, a mirror, or a house.
normal.cn: furbish 常接旧物作宾语：刀剑、镜子或房屋。

abstract.en: See a cloth rubbing a brass plate until it throws back light.
abstract.cn: 想象一块布反复擦拭铜盘，直到它把光反回来。

abstract.en: See a dusty mirror in a workshop, its frame wiped clean.
abstract.cn: 想象作坊里一面落灰的镜子，镜框被擦得干干净净。

abstract.en: See an old notebook opened, its pages brightened by a fresh reading.
abstract.cn: 想象一本旧笔记被翻开，因重新阅读而重新明亮。

examples.en: The steward furbished the trophies before the ceremony.
examples.cn: 管理员在典礼前把奖杯擦亮了。

examples.en: A furbished lobby greeted the guests.
examples.cn: 翻新过的大堂迎接了客人。

examples.en: He furbished up his notes the night before the exam.
examples.cn: 考试前一夜他把笔记重新整理温习了一遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拂必拭」——要擦亮一件东西，「拂」过之后「必」定要「拭」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 forbir（擦亮、清洁）一般认为来自法兰克语重构形式 *furbjan（清洗）；中古英语借入为 furbish，核心义是「擦到发亮」。

sensesIntro.en: Furbish begins with the polishing of a surface, widens to restoring old things, moves to refreshing the mind, and ends in literary or deceptive gloss.
sensesIntro.cn: furbish 从擦亮表面开始，扩展到修复旧物，再转向更新头脑中的知识，最后落到文学化的修饰与带欺骗性的粉饰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloth rubbing an old surface until it shines.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块布把旧表面擦出光来。

branches.en: Plain polishing is the base sense.
branches.cn: 单纯的擦亮是基础义项。

branches.en: Restoring an old object extends the polish.
branches.cn: 修复旧物是擦亮的延伸。

branches.en: Refreshing knowledge moves the shine into the mind.
branches.cn: 温习知识把光泽移到头脑里。

branches.en: Smartening and deceptive gloss both work only on the surface.
branches.cn: 修饰与粉饰都只在表面做文章。

branches.en: Cleaning out and restoring share the old French sense.
branches.cn: 清除与修复共享古法语中的清洗义。

intro.en: Furbish is built on a French verb, and English adds a prefix and two suffixes around it.
intro.cn: furbish 以一个法语动词为基础，英语围绕它加了一个前缀和两个后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin etymon here: the line runs from Frankish through Old French forbir into English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语词源：它从法兰克语经古法语 forbir 进入英语。

items.exampleCN: 古法语 forbir 本义就是擦亮。

items.example: Furbish keeps the physical shine.
items.exampleCN: furbish 保留了物理上的光泽义。

items.example: She furbishes the silver every spring.
items.exampleCN: 她每年春天都把银器擦一遍。

items.example: The plate was furbished by hand.
items.exampleCN: 那面盘子是手工擦亮的。

items.example: He spent the morning furbishing the frames.
items.exampleCN: 他花了一上午擦亮画框。

items.example: Furbisher names the person who polishes.
items.exampleCN: furbisher 指从事擦亮的人。

items.example: Furbishment names the act itself.
items.exampleCN: furbishment 指擦亮这一行为。

items.example: The prefix re- adds the idea of repetition.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 添加「重复」的含义。

items.example: Refurbish means to furbish once more.
items.exampleCN: refurbish 指再擦亮、再翻新一次。

items.example: Refurbishment is the work of renovating.
items.exampleCN: refurbishment 指翻新的工作。

definition_zh: 供应；提供；为房间配置家具
definition_en: to provide something that is needed, or to equip a room with furniture
core_image: 把所需之物一件件搬进空房间，摆到该在的位置
scene: 房东为每间客房配好了桌椅和台灯。The landlord furnished every guest room with a desk and a lamp.
sceneCN: 这里 furnish 是「配置家具」（第 2 个义项：为房间装备家具）；句意：房东为每间客房配好了桌椅和台灯。

pos.zh: 供应；提供；配置家具

derivatives.zh: 过去分词作形容词，指配有家具的
动名词转名词，指家具陈设或供应行为
复数形式，指室内的陈设品与配件
动词加 -er 构成，指供应者或家具商

senses.title: To supply what is needed
senses.definition: to provide someone or something with what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 向某人或某物提供所需的东西
senses.example: The company furnishes tools to every new worker.
senses.exampleCN: 公司给每位新员工配备工具。
senses.why: Old French furnir meant to accomplish or provide, and supply is the broad base sense.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 furnir 意为完成或供应，「提供」正是最宽泛的基础义。

senses.title: To equip a room with furniture
senses.definition: to put furniture, fittings, and equipment into a room or building
senses.definitionCN: 把家具、装置与设备放进房间或建筑里
senses.example: They furnished the flat in a simple style.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把那套公寓布置成简洁的风格。
senses.why: The general act of supplying narrowed to the furnishing of a home, where the goods are visible.
senses.whyCN: 宽泛的供应行为收窄到「布置住所」，因为那里的物品看得见摸得着。

senses.title: To yield or produce
senses.definition: to produce or yield something as a natural result
senses.definitionCN: 作为自然结果产出或出产某物
senses.example: These orchards furnish apples for the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这些果园为整个山谷供应苹果。
senses.why: What the land supplies is what it yields, so supply shades into produce.
senses.whyCN: 土地所供应之物就是它所出产之物，于是「供应」自然滑向「出产」。

senses.title: To provide evidence or information
senses.definition: to give facts, evidence, or information to someone who needs it
senses.definitionCN: 向需要的人给出事实、证据或信息
senses.example: The witness furnished the court with a full account.
senses.exampleCN: 证人向法庭提供了完整的陈述。
senses.why: Official and legal supply became a fixed sense for documents, proof, and data.
senses.whyCN: 公文与法律中的「供应」固定为提供文件、证据与数据，于是有了这个义项。

senses.title: To serve as or contribute
senses.definition: to serve as something, or to add a quality to it
senses.definitionCN: 充当某物，或为某物增添一种性质
senses.example: The old walls furnish a fine example of local stonework.
senses.exampleCN: 这些旧墙构成了本地石作的绝佳范例。
senses.why: Something supplied can become the example or quality itself, so supply turns into contribution.
senses.whyCN: 被供应出来的东西本身可以成为范例或性质，于是「提供」转为「构成、贡献」。

senses.title: To fit out with equipment
senses.definition: to fit a ship, office, or workshop with the equipment it needs
senses.definitionCN: 为船只、办公室或车间配备所需的器材
senses.example: The workshop was furnished with modern looms.
senses.exampleCN: 车间配备了现代化的织机。
senses.why: Equipment supply extends the room sense from homes to ships and workplaces.
senses.whyCN: 器材供应把「布置房间」的义项从住宅扩展到船只与工作场所。

intro.en: Furnish comes through Old French furnir, to accomplish or provide, from a reconstructed Frankish verb.
intro.cn: furnish 经古法语 furnir（完成、供应）而来，其源头是重构的法兰克语动词。

items.en: A reconstructed verb, frumjan, means to further or accomplish.
items.cn: 重构形式 frumjan，意为推进或完成。

items.en: Furnir means to accomplish, to provide.
items.cn: furnir 意为完成、供应。

items.en: Furnish enters English as to supply.
items.cn: furnish 在十四世纪进入英语，意为供应。

items.en: The verb comes to mean equipping a room.
items.cn: 这个动词开始表示布置房间。

items.en: Furnish evidence and data become standard phrases.
items.cn: furnish evidence 与 furnish data 成为固定说法。

note.en: Furnish is the verb behind furniture, and it stands beside the ordinary supply verbs.
note.cn: furnish 是 furniture 背后的动词，并与常见的「供应」类动词相邻。

entries.definition: the movable goods that equip a room
entries.definitionCN: 装备房间的可移动家具

entries.definition: supplied or equipped
the act of supplying or equipping

to deliver goods or materials

normalIntro.en: Furnish names the act of supplying, and its family reaches from tools and evidence to the furniture of a room.
normalIntro.cn: furnish 指供应这一行为，它的词族从工具、证据一直延伸到房间里的家具。

normal.en: Furnish and furniture share one origin: the verb names the act, the noun the goods.
normal.cn: furnish 与 furniture 同源：动词指行为，名词指物品。

normal.en: Furnish with is the key pattern: furnish a room with chairs.
normal.cn: furnish with 是关键句式：用椅子布置房间。

normal.en: The family runs furnish, furnished, furnishing, furnishings.
normal.cn: 词族包括 furnish、furnished、furnishing、furnishings。

normal.en: Furnish also supplies abstract things: information, evidence, proof.
normal.cn: furnish 也能供应抽象之物：信息、证据、证明。

normal.en: Contrast furnish and provide: furnish often fits rooms and official documents.
normal.cn: 对比 furnish 与 provide：furnish 更常搭配房间与正式文件。

abstract.cn: 想象一箱箱物资被搬进空荡荡的大厅。

abstract.en: See chairs and tables placed into a bare room.
abstract.cn: 想象桌椅被摆进一间空屋。

abstract.en: See an orchard so loaded that it supplies the whole valley.
abstract.cn: 想象果园结满果实，供应整个山谷。

examples.en: The company furnishes tools to every new worker.
examples.cn: 公司给每位新员工配备工具。

examples.en: They furnished the flat in a simple style.

examples.en: The witness furnished the court with a full account.

root: 古法语 furnir（完成、供应）一般认为来自法兰克语重构形式 *frumjan（促成）；中古英语借入为 furnish，核心义是「把所需之物送到位」。

sensesIntro.en: Furnish begins with general supply, narrows to equipping a room, and spreads out again to harvests, evidence, examples, and workshops.
sensesIntro.cn: furnish 从一般的「供应」出发，收窄为「布置房间」，再向外扩展到收成、证据、范例与车间器材。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: needed goods carried in and put in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：把所需之物搬进来并各就各位。

branches.en: General supply is the base sense.
branches.cn: 泛泛的供应是基础义项。

branches.en: Furnishing a room is supply made visible.
branches.cn: 布置房间是看得见的供应。

branches.en: Yielding is supply from land or nature.
branches.cn: 出产是土地或自然的供应。

branches.en: Documents and examples are intangible things supplied.
branches.cn: 文件与范例都是被供应出来的无形之物。

branches.en: Room and workplace equipment form one equipment branch.
branches.cn: 房间布置与车间器材构成同一个「装备」分支。

intro.en: Furnish is a French-derived verb whose English family includes furniture, furnishings, and the negative unfurnished.
intro.cn: furnish 是来自法语的动词，其英语词族包括 furniture、furnishings 以及反义的 unfurnished。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin furnire is generally taken as a borrowing back from Old French furnir, so the Latin link is secondary.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 furnire 一般被视为从古法语 furnir 回借而来，因此拉丁语这一环是次要的。

items.example: Furnish keeps the broad supply sense.
items.exampleCN: furnish 保留了宽泛的供应义。

items.example: The firm furnishes uniforms each year.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司每年供应制服。

items.example: The room was furnished in oak.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间用橡木家具布置。

items.example: They are furnishing the new office.
items.exampleCN: 他们正在布置新办公室。

items.example: Furnisher names the one who supplies.
items.exampleCN: furnisher 指提供货物的人。

items.example: Furniture is the goods that furnish.
items.exampleCN: furniture 就是用来布置的物件。

items.example: Furnishings are the smaller fittings.
items.exampleCN: furnishings 指较小的陈设与配件。

items.example: The prefix un- negates the participle.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 使分词变为否定。

items.example: Unfurnished means bare of furniture.
items.exampleCN: unfurnished 指没有配备家具。

definition_zh: 家具；设备；陈设
definition_en: the movable articles that make a room fit for living or working
core_image: 空屋子里搬进的桌、椅、床、柜
scene: 搬家那天，所有家具都从卡车上卸了下来。On moving day all the furniture came down from the truck.
sceneCN: 这里 furniture 是「家具」（第 1 个义项：房间里的可移动陈设）；句意：搬家那天，所有家具都从卡车上卸了下来。

senses.title: Movable articles in a room
senses.definition: the tables, chairs, beds, and cabinets that equip a room
senses.definitionCN: 装备房间的桌子、椅子、床与柜子等可移动物件
senses.example: The flat came with all its furniture.
senses.exampleCN: 这套公寓连同全部家具一起交付。
senses.why: Old French fourniture meant equipment, and household equipment became the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 fourniture 意为装备，家用装备逐渐成为最日常的义项。

senses.title: The gear of a ship or machine
senses.definition: the fittings and gear of a ship, or the equipment of a machine
senses.definitionCN: 船只的附属装置与用具，或机器的设备
senses.example: The crew stowed the deck furniture before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 船员在暴风雨前把甲板用具收好。
senses.why: Equipment was the original meaning, so ships and machines kept the older, wider sense.
senses.whyCN: 「装备」本是原义，船只与机器保留了这个更古老、更宽泛的义项。

senses.title: Blank blocks in letterpress printing
senses.definition: blocks and spaces used to fill a page in letterpress printing
senses.definitionCN: 凸版印刷中用来填满版面的木块与空材
senses.example: The printer locked the furniture into the forme.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷工把填空木块锁进版框中。
senses.why: Printing called its blank blocks by the same equipment word, because they fill out the page.
senses.whyCN: 印刷业用它称呼填空木块，因为这些材料正是把版面「装备」齐全。

senses.title: Fittings in a public space
senses.definition: the benches, signs, and fixtures installed in a street or public place
senses.definitionCN: 安装在街道或公共场所的长椅、标志与固定设施
senses.example: The council renewed the street furniture along the promenade.
senses.exampleCN: 市政部门更新了海滨步道旁的街道设施。
senses.why: Urban design borrowed the household word for the fittings of a public room, the street.
senses.whyCN: 城市设计借用了这个家居词，指公共「房间」即街道里的固定设施。

senses.title: Mental equipment, in older use
senses.definition: the accomplishments and knowledge that equip a mind, in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中指装备头脑的学识与才艺
senses.example: Grammar and rhetoric were once the furniture of an educated mind.
senses.exampleCN: 语法与修辞曾被视为受教育者头脑中的必备装备。
senses.why: The equipment image moved from rooms to minds, a usage now archaic but still readable.
senses.whyCN: 「装备」的意象从房间移到头脑，这个用法如今古旧，但仍可理解。

normal.en: Furniture is uncountable: say a piece of furniture, not a furniture.
normal.cn: furniture 不可数：要说 a piece of furniture，不能说 a furniture。

normal.en: The family runs furnish, furnished, furnishing, furnishings.
normal.cn: 词族包括 furnish、furnished、furnishing、furnishings。

normal.en: Street furniture names public fittings such as benches and signs.
normal.cn: street furniture 指长椅、标志等公共设施。

normal.en: In printing, furniture means the blank blocks that fill a forme.
normal.cn: 在印刷业，furniture 指填满版框的空白木块。

abstract.en: See a truck unload tables and chairs into an empty room.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆卡车把桌椅卸进空房间。

abstract.en: See deck gear stowed neatly before a storm.
abstract.cn: 想象暴风雨前甲板用具被整齐收好。

abstract.en: See a printer locking blank blocks into a forme.
abstract.cn: 想象印刷工把空白木块锁进版框。

examples.en: The flat came with all its furniture.
examples.cn: 这套公寓连同全部家具一起交付。

examples.en: They bought a piece of furniture for the hall.
examples.cn: 他们为门厅买了一件家具。

examples.en: The council replaced the street furniture after the floods.
examples.cn: 洪灾过后市政部门更换了街道设施。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「房内饰」——「房」子「内」部的陈「饰」，正是家具；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 fourniture（供应、装备）来自 fournir（供应）；中世纪拉丁语 furnitura 一般视为回借形式；英语 furniture 本指「装备」，十七世纪起专指家具。

sensesIntro.en: Furniture begins as equipment of any kind, settles on household goods, and keeps older technical senses in ships, printing, streets, and minds.
sensesIntro.cn: furniture 起初泛指各种装备，后来落定于家居物品，同时在船只、印刷、街道与头脑中保留了较古老的技术义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: goods brought in to equip a bare room.
core.cn: 核心意象：把物件搬进来，装备一间空屋。

branches.en: Household goods are the everyday core.
branches.cn: 家居物品是日常的核心义。

branches.en: Ship and machine gear keep the wide equipment sense.
branches.cn: 船具与机器装置保留了宽泛的装备义。

branches.en: Printing blocks are equipment for a page.
branches.cn: 印刷木块是装备版面的器材。

branches.en: Street fittings equip a public room.
branches.cn: 街道设施装备的是公共空间。

branches.en: A room and a mind are both equipped by furniture.
branches.cn: 房间与头脑都可以被「家具」装备。

intro.en: Furniture is a French-derived noun built on fournir, with an English family of verbs, adjectives, and compounds.
intro.cn: furniture 是来自法语的名词，建立在 fournir 之上，英语中形成了动词、形容词与复合词词族。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin furnitura means a supplying and is generally treated as a borrowing from French, not as the origin.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 furnitura 意为供应，一般被视为借自法语，而不是源头。

items.example: Fourniture is the direct source of furniture.
items.exampleCN: fourniture 是 furniture 的直接来源。

items.example: Furnir supplies the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: furnir 提供了名词背后的动词。

items.example: Furnish keeps the act of supplying.
items.exampleCN: furnish 保留了供应的行为义。

items.example: Furniture narrows to household goods.
items.exampleCN: furniture 收窄为家居物品。

items.example: Furnished describes a ready room.
items.exampleCN: furnished 描述已经配好家具的房间。

items.example: Furnishing names the work of equipping.
items.exampleCN: furnishing 指装备布置这件事。

items.example: Furnishings are the smaller pieces.
items.exampleCN: furnishings 指较小的陈设件。

items.meaningCN: 表示结果或行为的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ure turns a verb into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ure 把动词变成名词。

items.example: Furnitureless adds a negative suffix.
items.exampleCN: furnitureless 加了否定后缀。

items.example: Street furniture extends the word outdoors.
items.exampleCN: street furniture 把词义扩展到户外。

definition_zh: 此外；而且；再者
definition_en: in addition to what has just been said
core_image: 已经往前走了一步，又往前多迈一步
scene: 报告已经说明成本很高，接着又补充了工期风险。The report had already noted the high cost; furthermore, it warned of delays.
sceneCN: 这里 furthermore 是「此外」（第 1 个义项：在已说的内容上再加一点）；句意：报告已经说明成本很高，接着又补充了工期风险。

pos.zh: 此外；而且；再者

derivatives.zh: 比较级形式，指更远的；进一步的
加 -ance 构成，指促进、推进
加 -most 构成，指最远的

senses.title: Adding another point
senses.definition: used to add another point to what has just been said
senses.definitionCN: 用于在刚说过的内容上再补充一点
senses.example: The plan is cheap; furthermore, it is quick to build.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案成本低；此外，建造起来也很快。
senses.why: Further means to a greater extent, and more adds one more item, so the word literally piles one point on another.
senses.whyCN: further 表示「更进一步」，more 表示「更多」，这个词字面上就是把一点再加到另一点上。

senses.title: Adding a stronger claim
senses.definition: used to introduce a statement that strengthens or sharpens the previous one
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出一个加强或加剧前句的陈述
senses.example: The scheme failed; furthermore, it left the town in debt.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划失败了；更有甚者，它让小镇背上了债务。
senses.why: The added step can be a heavier one, so simple addition becomes escalation.
senses.whyCN: 加上去的那一步可以更重，于是单纯的「补充」变成了「升级、加剧」。

senses.title: Adding the next item in a list
senses.definition: used to add a new item to a list or a series
senses.definitionCN: 用于向清单或序列中再加入一项
senses.example: The form asks for a name, an address, and furthermore a signature.
senses.exampleCN: 表格要求填写姓名、地址，另外还要签名。
senses.why: The word works as a list marker, moving the reader from one item to the next.
senses.whyCN: 这个词充当清单标记，把读者从一项带到下一项。

senses.title: Signposting an academic argument
senses.definition: used in formal or academic prose to advance an argument
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或学术文章中用于推进论证
senses.example: Furthermore, the experiment must be repeated before any conclusion is drawn.
senses.exampleCN: 此外，在得出任何结论之前必须重做这项实验。
senses.why: Academic writing adopts the word as a signpost of cumulative reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 学术写作把这个词当作路标，表示论证正在层层累积。

senses.title: Chaining a step in a proof
senses.definition: used in a proof or a formal argument to add the next step of reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 在证明或形式论证中用于接上下一步推理
senses.example: Furthermore, every prime greater than two is odd.
senses.exampleCN: 进而，每个大于二的素数都是奇数。
senses.why: Proof style treats each added line as a further step, so the additive word becomes a logical link.
senses.whyCN: 证明体把每一条新增的陈述都视为「再往前一步」，于是这个补充词成了逻辑连接。

intro.en: Furthermore is a native English compound of further and more, and further goes back to Old English furðor, the comparative of forth.
intro.cn: furthermore 是 further 与 more 构成的英语本族复合词，而 further 可追溯到古英语 furðor，即 forth 的比较级。

items.en: Furðor is the comparative of forth, meaning more forward.
items.cn: furðor 是 forth 的比较级，意为更向前。

items.en: Further works as an adverb of distance and degree.
items.cn: further 作副词，表示距离与程度。

items.en: Furthermore appears with the sense of in addition.
items.cn: furthermore 出现，意为「此外」。

items.en: Academic and legal prose adopt it as a signpost.
items.cn: 学术与法律文章把它采纳为路标词。

items.en: Exam writing uses it to chain formal points.
items.cn: 考试写作用它串联正式论点。

note.en: Furthermore belongs to the further family and stands beside the formal additive adverbs.
note.cn: furthermore 属于 further 词族，并与正式的「补充」类副词相邻。

entries.definition: to a greater distance or extent
the act of promoting something
most distant
in addition, and often with a stronger point
entries.definitionCN: 此外，且常引出更强的论点

entries.definition: in addition, used in looser speech
entries.definitionCN: 此外，多用于较随意的口语

entries.definition: as an extra thing

normalIntro.en: Furthermore is further plus more: one more step beyond what has already been said.
normalIntro.cn: furthermore 就是 further 加 more：在已说之处再往前多走一步。

normal.en: Furthermore is literally further plus more, so it adds one more point.
normal.cn: furthermore 字面上就是 further 加 more，所以它是再补一点。

normal.en: It is formal: in speech people usually say besides or also.
normal.cn: 它偏正式；口语里人们通常说 besides 或 also。

normal.en: The family includes further, furtherance, and furthermost.
normal.cn: 词族包括 further、furtherance 与 furthermost。

normal.en: Use a comma after furthermore when it opens a sentence.
normal.cn: furthermore 位于句首时，后面要加逗号。

normal.en: Compare moreover: both are formal adders, but moreover often adds a stronger claim.
normal.cn: 对比 moreover：两者都是正式补充词，但 moreover 常引出更强的论点。

abstract.en: See a walker take one more pace along a straight path.
abstract.cn: 想象行路人在直道上又向前迈出一步。

abstract.en: See another weight laid on a scale that is already loaded.
abstract.cn: 想象已经载重的天平上又加了一块砝码。

abstract.en: See a new line written at the foot of a list.
abstract.cn: 想象清单末尾又添上新的一行。

examples.en: The plan is cheap; furthermore, it is quick to build.
examples.cn: 这个方案成本低；此外，建造起来也很快。

examples.en: Furthermore, the experiment must be repeated before any conclusion is drawn.
examples.cn: 此外，在得出任何结论之前必须重做这项实验。

examples.en: The rent is due monthly; furthermore, the tenant must insure the flat.
examples.cn: 房租按月支付；此外，房客还必须为公寓投保。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「further more」——已经更「远」，还要更「多」，一层层加上去；这只是拆词联想，与词源考证无关。

root: 古英语 furðor 是 forth（向前）的比较级，意为「更向前」；further 加 more 构成 furthermore，字面即「再往前多一层」，十六世纪起用作「此外」。

sensesIntro.en: Furthermore adds a plain point, then a stronger claim, then a list item, and finally serves as a signpost in academic prose and in proofs.
sensesIntro.cn: furthermore 先补一个普通论点，再引一个更强的说法，再接一个清单项，最后成为学术文章与证明中的路标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one more step forward on a path already begun.
core.cn: 核心意象：在已经走上的路上再向前一步。

branches.en: Plain addition is the base sense.
branches.cn: 普通的补充是基础义项。

branches.en: A stronger claim is addition with weight.
branches.cn: 更强的论点就是带重量的补充。

branches.en: A list item is addition in sequence.
branches.cn: 清单项是按顺序的补充。

branches.en: Academic prose and proofs use it as a reasoning signpost.
branches.cn: 学术文章与证明把它当作推理路标。

branches.en: The same additive core serves both prose and lists.
branches.cn: 同一个补充核心同时服务于行文与清单。

intro.en: Furthermore is a native compound, built from the comparative further and the native word more.
intro.cn: furthermore 是本族复合词，由比较级 further 与本族词 more 构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin etymon here: further comes from Old English furðor, and more is likewise native.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语词源：further 来自古英语 furðor，more 同样是本族词。

items.example: Forth is the simple adverb of forward movement.
items.exampleCN: forth 是表示向前的简单副词。

items.example: Furðor is the comparative of forth.
items.exampleCN: furðor 是 forth 的比较级。

items.example: Further describes a greater distance.
items.exampleCN: further 描述更远的距离。

items.example: Further also marks a greater degree.
items.exampleCN: further 也标记更高的程度。

items.example: Furthermore joins one point to the next.
items.exampleCN: furthermore 把一点接到下一点。

items.example: Furtherance names the act of advancing.
items.exampleCN: furtherance 指推进这一行为。

items.example: Furthermost is the superlative of place.
items.exampleCN: furthermost 是位置上的最高级。

items.example: Furthering is the work of advancing a cause.
items.exampleCN: furthering 指推进某项事业。

items.meaningCN: 更多（在复合词中表示程度）
items.example: More adds degree inside the compound.
items.exampleCN: more 在复合词中增加程度。

definition_zh: 偷偷摸摸的；鬼鬼祟祟的；暗中进行的
definition_en: done quietly and secretly so that other people will not see or notice it
core_image: 一只手把东西悄悄塞进口袋，眼睛还在四处打量
scene: 深夜的走廊里，有人贴着墙根快步溜过，还不停回头张望。A man slipped along the dark corridor, casting a furtive glance at every door.
sceneCN: 这里 furtive 是「鬼鬼祟祟的」（第 1 个义项：为避免被注意而偷偷行动）；句意：一个人沿着昏暗的走廊溜过去，朝每一扇门偷偷瞟了一眼。

pos.zh: 偷偷摸摸的；鬼鬼祟祟的；暗中进行的

derivatives.zh: 由 furtive 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「偷偷地；鬼祟地」
由 furtive 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「鬼祟；隐秘」
与 furtive 同出拉丁语 fur（小偷），经法语指用来捕兔的雪貂

senses.title: Secretive action to avoid being noticed
senses.definition: done in a quiet, secret way so that other people will not see or notice it
senses.definitionCN: 以安静而秘密的方式做，以免被别人看见或注意
senses.example: He took a furtive step towards the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他偷偷朝门口挪了一步。
senses.why: The Latin adjective furtivus means stolen, so a furtive act is one that seems to be stolen away from other eyes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语形容词 furtivus 意为「偷来的」，所以 furtive 的动作像是从别人眼皮底下偷走的。

senses.title: A quick sideways glance
senses.definition: a short look that darts sideways, as if the person is checking whether anyone is watching
senses.definitionCN: 迅速斜过去的一眼，像是在确认有没有人在看
senses.example: She gave the letters a furtive glance and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 她偷偷瞟了一眼那些信，什么也没说。
senses.why: A glance is the smallest visible piece of a secret, so the adjective attaches itself to the eyes first.
senses.whyCN: 眼神是秘密最小的一块可见碎片，所以这个词最先落在眼睛上。

senses.title: A person who seems to hide something
senses.titleCN: 行迹可疑的；躲躲闪闪的
senses.definition: behaving in a way that suggests a hidden purpose or a secret to protect
senses.definitionCN: 举止让人觉出别有目的，或者有事要瞒
senses.example: The furtive man in the corner never once looked at the menu.
senses.exampleCN: 角落里那个躲躲闪闪的男人一次也没看菜单。
senses.why: When the secret action becomes a habit, the adjective moves from the act to the person who performs it.
senses.whyCN: 当偷偷的行动变成习惯，这个词就从动作转到做动作的人身上。

senses.title: Stealthy movement in the dark
senses.definition: moving softly and slowly, the way a thief moves through a dark house
senses.definitionCN: 轻轻地、缓慢地移动，像小偷在漆黑的房子里走动
senses.example: A furtive figure slipped between the parked cars.
senses.exampleCN: 一个鬼祟的身影在停着的车之间溜过。
senses.why: The thief at the heart of the word supplies its most physical sense: movement that makes almost no sound.
senses.whyCN: 词源里的小偷提供了最具体的一层意思：几乎不发出声音的移动。

senses.title: A stolen-seeming gesture
senses.definition: an act such as a kiss or a touch that is given quickly and kept out of sight
senses.definitionCN: 如亲吻或触碰这类快速给出、又不让人看见的举动
senses.example: They exchanged a furtive kiss behind the curtain.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在帘子后面偷偷吻了一下。
senses.why: Because furtivus literally means stolen, any gesture that feels taken rather than given can be called furtive.
senses.whyCN: 因为 furtivus 字面就是「被偷走的」，任何像是被夺取而不是被给予的举动都能用这个词。

senses.title: A secretly cherished feeling
senses.titleCN: 暗自怀有的希望或喜悦
senses.definition: a hope or pleasure that a person keeps to themselves and does not admit openly
senses.definitionCN: 一个人藏在心里、不公开承认的希望或喜悦
senses.example: He felt a furtive pleasure at the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息，他心里暗暗高兴。
senses.why: Once the word names hidden things, it can also name hidden feelings, kept from view like stolen goods.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词能指藏起来的东西，也就能指藏起来的情绪，它们像赃物一样被收了起来。

intro.en: Furtive reaches English through French from Latin furtivus, an adjective built on fur, the word for a thief.
intro.cn: furtive 经法语进入英语，源头是拉丁语 furtivus，由表示「小偷」的 fur 构成。

items.en: Fur is the Latin noun for a thief.
items.cn: fur 是拉丁语中表示「小偷」的名词。

items.en: Furtum means a theft, something taken secretly.
items.cn: furtum 意为偷窃，指被偷偷拿走的东西。

items.en: Furtivus, built on furtum, means stolen or done by stealth.
items.cn: 由 furtum 构成的 furtivus 意为「偷来的」或「暗中做的」。

items.en: Furtif carries the adjective into French with the same secret sense.
items.cn: furtif 把这个形容词带进法语，秘密的含义不变。

items.en: Furtive is recorded in English in the seventeenth century for stealthy behaviour.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语中已有 furtive，用来形容鬼祟的举止。

items.en: Modern English extends it to glances, gestures, feelings and even hopes.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到眼神、举动、情绪乃至希望。

note.en: Furtive belongs to the Latin thief family and sits close to stealthy, secretive and clandestine.
note.cn: furtive 属于拉丁语「小偷」词族，与 stealthy、secretive、clandestine 意义相邻。

entries.definition: a small animal used for hunting rabbits, whose Latin name also means thief
entries.definitionCN: 用来捕兔的雪貂，其拉丁语名称同样意为小偷

entries.definition: in a secretive, sneaking way
the quality of acting as if something is hidden
moving or acting quietly so as not to be detected
entries.definitionCN: 悄悄的；动作轻而不易被察觉的

entries.definition: tending to keep information or intentions hidden
entries.definitionCN: 爱保密的；不轻易透露的

entries.definition: kept secret, especially because it is not allowed
entries.definitionCN: 秘密的；尤指因不合规而暗中的

normalIntro.en: Furtive is a thief word: its Latin root names the person who takes things secretly.
normalIntro.cn: furtive 是一个小偷词：它的拉丁词根指的就是偷偷拿东西的人。

normal.en: Latin fur means thief, so furtive describes behaviour that looks like stealing.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 fur 意为小偷，所以 furtive 形容像偷东西一样的举止。

normal.en: A furtive glance is the quick look of someone with something to hide.
normal.cn: 「a furtive glance」就是有秘密的人那种飞快的一瞥。

normal.en: Furtively and furtiveness are the adverb and noun built on the same stem.
normal.cn: furtively 与 furtiveness 是同一词干上的副词和名词。

normal.en: Stealthy stresses quiet movement, while furtive stresses not wanting to be seen.
normal.cn: stealthy 强调动作轻，furtive 强调不想被看见。

normal.en: In a furtive manner is simply a formal way of saying secretly.
normal.cn: 「in a furtive manner」只是「偷偷地」的正式说法。

abstract.en: Picture a hand sliding a note into a pocket while the eyes check the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把纸条塞进口袋，眼睛还在打量房间。

abstract.en: Picture a glance that darts to the door and back in half a second.
abstract.cn: 想象一道目光在半秒内瞟向门口又收回来。

abstract.en: Picture a cat crossing a fence at night on silent paws.
abstract.cn: 想象一只猫在夜里踩着无声的步子越过篱笆。

examples.en: She cast a furtive glance at the letter on the desk.
examples.cn: 她偷偷瞟了一眼桌上的信。

examples.en: The two men exchanged furtive whispers by the gate.
examples.cn: 那两个人在大门边偷偷低语。

examples.en: He made a furtive attempt to hide the key in his palm.
examples.cn: 他偷偷把钥匙藏进手心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「福提武」——像小偷提着赃物快步走开，所以是偷偷摸摸的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fur（小偷）→ furtum（偷窃）→ furtivus（偷来的、秘密的）→ 古法语 furtif → 英语 furtive，核心义是「像小偷一样不让人看见」。

sensesIntro.en: Furtive starts from a stolen action, narrows to a darting glance, then widens to a suspicious person, silent movement, stolen-seeming gestures and hidden feelings.
sensesIntro.cn: furtive 从「偷来的动作」出发，收窄到飞快的一瞥，再扩展到可疑的人、无声的移动、像偷来的举动以及藏起来的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand slipping something out of sight while the eyes watch the room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把东西悄悄藏起来，眼睛还在留意四周。

branches.en: The core sense is any act done so as not to be noticed.
branches.cn: 核心义项是任何为了避免被注意而做的动作。

branches.en: A furtive glance is the smallest visible sign of a secret.
branches.cn: 偷偷的一瞥是秘密露出的最小可见痕迹。

branches.en: A furtive person is one whose whole manner suggests a hidden aim.
branches.cn: 鬼祟的人整个举止都暗示着另有目的。

branches.en: Both a quiet step and a stolen kiss are actions kept from other eyes.
branches.cn: 悄悄的一步和偷来的一个吻，都是避开他人目光的动作。

branches.en: Silent movement and a secret hope are both kept out of sight, one in space and one in the mind.
branches.cn: 无声的移动和暗藏的希望都被藏了起来，一个藏在空间里，一个藏在心里。

intro.en: Furtive is built on the Latin thief family, with English adverbs and nouns added around it.
intro.cn: furtive 建立在拉丁语「小偷」词族之上，英语又围绕它构成副词和名词。
