latinIntro.en: Latin fur means thief, furtum means theft, and furtivus means stolen or secret.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fur 意为小偷，furtum 意为偷窃，furtivus 意为偷来的或秘密的。

items.example: Fur is the thief at the root of the family.
items.exampleCN: fur 是这个词族根部的小偷。

items.example: Furtum names the act of taking something secretly.
items.exampleCN: furtum 指偷偷拿走东西的行为。

items.example: Furtivus gives the adjective its secret sense.
items.exampleCN: furtivus 给这个形容词秘密的含义。

items.example: Old French furtif shortens the Latin form.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 furtif 缩短了拉丁语形式。

items.example: Furtive enters English with the French shape.
items.exampleCN: furtive 带着法语形态进入英语。

items.example: The adverb ending marks how the act is done.
items.exampleCN: 副词词尾标明动作进行的方式。

items.example: The noun ending names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: 名词词尾直接指这种性质。

items.meaning: tending to, having the nature of
items.example: The suffix -ive makes an adjective of tendency.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成表示倾向的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns adjectives into adverbs.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成副词。

items.meaning: a small animal used to hunt rabbits
items.example: Ferret comes from the same Latin thief through its French name.
items.exampleCN: ferret 经法语名称来自同一个拉丁语「小偷」。

definition_zh: 大惊小怪；忙乱；争吵；小题大做
definition_en: unnecessary excitement, worry, or activity about something unimportant
core_image: 一锅本来安静的水被人不停搅动，溅得灶台到处都是
scene: 餐厅里汤只是凉了一点，那位客人却把服务员叫来抱怨了半天。The guest made a fuss about the cold soup and called the manager twice.
sceneCN: 这里 fuss 是「大惊小怪」（第 1 个义项：为小事表现出过度的激动或抱怨）；句意：那位客人为了凉了的汤大吵大闹，还两次叫来经理。

pos.zh: 大惊小怪；忙乱；争吵
小题大做；瞎操心；烦躁哭闹

derivatives.zh: 由 fuss 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「爱挑剔的；过分讲究的」
由 fussy 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「挑剔地；小题大做地」
由 fussy 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「挑剔；繁琐」
fuss 与 budget 复合而成，口语指「爱挑剔、爱操心的人」

senses.title: Unnecessary excitement about a small matter
senses.definition: too much excitement, worry, or complaint about something that hardly matters
senses.definitionCN: 对几乎不重要的事表现出过多的激动、担心或抱怨
senses.example: There is no need to make such a fuss over a broken cup.
senses.exampleCN: 不过碎了个杯子，没必要这么大惊小怪。
senses.why: The word seems to echo the sound of people sputtering about nothing, so noisy excitement is built into its shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词听上去像人为了小事急得直嚷嚷的声音，所以「吵闹的激动」本就长在它的形状里。

senses.title: Noisy bustle and running about
senses.definition: a lot of hurried, noisy activity that produces little real result
senses.definitionCN: 大量匆忙而嘈杂的活动，实际成果却很少
senses.example: The fuss of moving house left everyone exhausted.
senses.exampleCN: 搬家的一通忙乱把所有人都累坏了。
senses.why: From excitement about nothing, the word slides easily to the noise and running about itself.
senses.whyCN: 从「为小事激动」很容易滑向那份嘈杂与来回奔走本身。

senses.title: A loud complaint or quarrel
senses.definition: a noisy argument or public complaint, often about something trivial
senses.definitionCN: 吵闹的争执或公开抱怨，往往为的只是小事
senses.example: The neighbours had a fuss about a parking space.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们为了一个车位吵了一通。
senses.why: A fuss made out loud in front of other people turns into a complaint or a quarrel.
senses.whyCN: 当着别人大声闹出来的 fuss，就变成了一场抱怨或争吵。

senses.title: To complain or worry about trifles
senses.definition: to complain, worry, or get excited about something that is not important
senses.definitionCN: 为不重要的事抱怨、担心或激动
senses.example: Do not fuss about the seating plan; nobody will notice.
senses.exampleCN: 别为座位安排瞎操心了，没人会在意。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an action: to fuss is to produce that unnecessary excitement yourself.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：to fuss 就是自己去制造那份多余的激动。

senses.title: To busy oneself with pointless little tasks
senses.definition: to move about busily doing small, often unnecessary things
senses.definitionCN: 忙忙碌碌地做琐碎而常常没有必要的事
senses.example: She fussed in the kitchen while the guests waited.
senses.exampleCN: 客人在等，她却在厨房里忙前忙后。
senses.why: Someone in a fuss is usually rushing about, so the verb also names pointless busy movement.
senses.whyCN: 陷在 fuss 里的人总是在来回奔忙，所以动词也指这种没有必要的忙乱。

senses.title: To give someone too much anxious care
senses.definition: to pay anxious, excessive attention to a person, especially a child or a guest
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、尤其是孩子或客人，给予过分紧张的照顾
senses.example: Grandmother fusses over the baby all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母整个下午都围着宝宝过分张罗。
senses.why: Caring for a person can turn into a fuss, because the attention becomes louder than the need.
senses.whyCN: 照顾一个人也会变成 fuss，因为那份关注比实际需要更喧闹。

senses.title: To cry and be restless, of a baby
senses.definition: of a baby, to cry, squirm, and refuse to settle
senses.definitionCN: 指婴儿哭闹、扭动、怎么也不肯安静下来
senses.example: The baby fussed all night and kept the whole house awake.
senses.exampleCN: 宝宝整夜哭闹，吵得一家人都没睡。
senses.why: A restless crying baby makes the same noise of distress, so parents say the baby is fussing.
senses.whyCN: 烦躁哭闹的婴儿发出同样是难受的声响，于是父母就说宝宝在 fussing。

intro.en: Fuss appears in English in the late eighteenth century, and no Latin or French source can be traced with confidence.
intro.cn: fuss 在十八世纪后期才出现在英语中，无法可靠地追溯到拉丁语或法语来源。

items.en: Fuss is first recorded in written English in the late eighteenth century.
items.cn: fuss 在十八世纪后期的书面英语中首次出现。

items.en: Dictionaries agree that the origin is uncertain; no Latin or French source is accepted.
items.cn: 各家词典一致认为来源不确定，没有公认的拉丁语或法语源头。

items.en: Most reference works treat it as echoic, imitating the sound of a sputtering bustle.
items.cn: 多数辞书把它看作拟声词，模仿忙乱时急促嘈杂的声响。

items.en: During the nineteenth century the noun widens to mean a noisy quarrel or complaint.
items.cn: 十九世纪时，这个名词扩展为指吵闹的争吵或抱怨。

items.en: Fussy, fussily, fussiness and the verb fuss all grow from the same short stem.
items.cn: fussy、fussily、fussiness 以及动词 fuss 都从同一个短词干长出来。

note.en: Fuss is a short echoic word for noisy bother, and its family is fussy, fussily and fussiness.
note.cn: fuss 是表示「吵闹的折腾」的短拟声词，它的词族是 fussy、fussily 与 fussiness。

entries.definition: hard to please or overly concerned with small details
entries.definitionCN: 爱挑剔的；过分讲究细节的

entries.definition: in a picky or overcareful manner
the quality of being hard to please
a noisy disturbance or confused movement
unnecessary activity and excitement about something trivial
entries.definitionCN: 为小事而白费的一番忙乱

entries.definition: unnecessary trouble taken over something small

normalIntro.en: Fuss is a short, noisy word, and English built its whole family on that one syllable.
normalIntro.cn: fuss 是一个又短又吵的词，英语的整个词族都建在这一个音节上。

normal.en: Fuss has no traced Latin source; it is most likely an echoic English coinage.
normal.cn: fuss 没有可追溯的拉丁语来源，很可能是英语里的拟声造词。

normal.en: Make a fuss is the most common pattern, and it names excitement about nothing.
normal.cn: 「make a fuss」是最常见的搭配，指为无谓的小事激动。

normal.en: Kick up a fuss adds the ideas of noise and public protest.
normal.cn: 「kick up a fuss」加上了吵闹与公开抗议的意味。

normal.en: Fuss over someone means giving that person too much anxious attention.
normal.cn: 「fuss over」某人，就是给那人过多紧张的关注。

normal.en: Fussy, fussily and fussiness grow from the same short stem.
normal.cn: fussy、fussily 与 fussiness 都从同一个短词干长出来。

abstract.en: Picture a pot of still water stirred until it splashes over the stove.
abstract.cn: 想象一锅安静的水被搅得泼出锅沿，弄脏整个灶台。

abstract.en: Picture a shop where three people run in circles for one missing receipt.
abstract.cn: 想象店里三个人为一张找不到的小票团团转。

abstract.en: Picture raised voices in a stairwell over a parking space.
abstract.cn: 想象楼道里为一处车位响起的争吵声。

examples.en: She made a fuss about the wrong date printed on the ticket.
examples.cn: 她为票上印错的日期大吵了一通。

examples.en: Stop fussing and let the child sleep.
examples.cn: 别瞎忙了，让孩子睡吧。

examples.en: They moved the whole office without any fuss.
examples.cn: 他们不声不响地搬完了整个办公室。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法事」——本来只是小事一桩，却像做法事一样折腾半天，就是大惊小怪；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定：一般认为 fuss 是十八世纪后期英语中的拟声造词，模仿忙乱时急促嘈杂的声响；先作名词「大惊小怪、忙乱」，再派生动词与形容词 fussy。

sensesIntro.en: Fuss begins with too much excitement about nothing, passes through bustle and quarrel, and then lives on in the verb: complain, rush about, over-care and cry.
sensesIntro.cn: fuss 从「为小事过度激动」开始，经过忙乱与争吵，再落到动词上：抱怨、来回忙、过分照顾以及婴儿哭闹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quiet pot of water stirred until it splashes everywhere.
core.cn: 核心意象：一锅安静的水被搅得四处溅开。

branches.en: The core sense is pointless excitement about a trivial thing.
branches.cn: 核心义项是为无足轻重的事白激动一场。

branches.en: The bustle sense names the noise and running itself.
branches.cn: 忙乱义项指的是那份嘈杂与奔走本身。

branches.en: A quarrel sense is a fuss performed in front of other people.
branches.cn: 争吵义项是在旁人面前演出来的那场 fuss。

branches.en: The verb splits into complaining about trifles and rushing about uselessly.
branches.cn: 动词分成两支：为小事抱怨，以及无意义地来回忙。

branches.en: Over-care for a person and a crying baby both show attention that will not settle.
branches.cn: 对某人过分照顾与婴儿哭闹，都表现为安顿不下来的关注。

intro.en: Fuss is a bare English stem, and its family is built with the suffixes -y, -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: fuss 是一个光秃秃的英语词干，它的词族靠 -y、-ly 与 -ness 三个后缀建成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source has been traced for fuss, so no Latin relatives are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: fuss 没有可追溯的拉丁语源头，因此这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: The noun fuss is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 名词 fuss 是整个词族的基础。

items.example: The verb fuss adds motion to the noun.
items.exampleCN: 动词 fuss 给名词加上了动作。

items.example: The suffix -y turns fuss into fussy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 fuss 变成 fussy。

items.example: Fussy describes a person full of fuss.
items.exampleCN: fussy 形容一个满是挑剔的人。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb fussily.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 fussily。

items.example: Fussily describes how a fussy person acts.
items.exampleCN: fussily 描述爱挑剔的人怎样行事。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms the noun fussiness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成名词 fussiness。

items.meaning: the quality of being hard to please
items.example: Fussiness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: fussiness 直接指这种性质。

items.meaning: a person who fusses about small things
items.example: Fussbudget joins fuss to an old word for a bag.
items.exampleCN: fussbudget 把 fuss 接到一个表示袋子的旧词上。

items.example: Fuss-free means free of fuss, with the suffix -free.
items.exampleCN: fuss-free 意为不含 fuss，用了后缀 -free。

definition_zh: 爱挑剔的；过分讲究的；繁琐的；（婴儿）烦躁的
definition_en: hard to please, or paying too much attention to small details
core_image: 有人把盘子里的每颗豆子都拨到一边，挑出不合心意的那一颗
scene: 点餐时她问了十遍配菜新不新鲜，还要把酱汁单独装在小碟里。At dinner she was so fussy that the waiter rewrote her order three times.
sceneCN: 这里 fussy 是「爱挑剔的」（第 1 个义项：对小事过分讲究、难以取悦）；句意：她在晚餐时挑剔到服务员把她的点单改了三次。

pos.zh: 爱挑剔的；过分讲究的；繁琐的；（婴儿）烦躁的

derivatives.zh: 由 fussy 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「挑剔地；过分讲究地」
由 fussy 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「挑剔；繁琐」
fussy 的词干，义为「大惊小怪；忙乱」，可作名词也可作动词
与 fussy 同源的复合名词，口语指「爱挑剔、爱操心的人」

senses.title: Hard to please about food or comfort
senses.definition: difficult to satisfy, especially about what one eats, wears, or how one is made comfortable
senses.definitionCN: 很难被满足，尤其在吃、穿或是否舒适这些事情上
senses.example: The child is a fussy eater and refuses all green vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 这孩子挑食，所有绿色的蔬菜都不吃。
senses.why: A person who makes a fuss about what is served is hard to please, so the adjective first names the choosy eater.
senses.whyCN: 为端上桌的东西大闹一场的人自然难伺候，所以这个词最先用来形容挑食的人。

senses.title: Overly concerned with small standards
senses.definition: giving too much attention to small details and to exact standards of correctness
senses.definitionCN: 对小细节和准确标准投入过多注意力
senses.example: She is fussy about how the towels are folded.
senses.exampleCN: 她对毛巾怎么叠极为讲究。
senses.why: Fuss is also the noise of unnecessary activity, and a fussy person turns that energy onto details and standards.
senses.whyCN: fuss 也指多余的忙乱，而爱挑剔的人把这份精力全用在细节和标准上。

senses.title: Over-decorated in design or dress
senses.definition: having too many decorative details, frills, or small ornaments
senses.definitionCN: 装饰细节、褶边或小饰物过多
senses.example: The fussy wallpaper made the small room feel crowded.
senses.exampleCN: 花哨的墙纸让这个小房间显得拥挤。
senses.why: When fuss spreads over an object, it becomes decoration piled on decoration, so the word reaches design.
senses.whyCN: 当 fuss 蔓延到物件上，就变成一层压一层的装饰，于是这个词进入了设计领域。

senses.title: Restless and crying, of a baby
senses.definition: crying, squirming, and refusing to settle, used of a baby or small child
senses.definitionCN: 指婴儿或幼儿哭闹、扭动、怎么也不肯安静下来
senses.example: The fussy baby calmed down only when her father held her.
senses.exampleCN: 这个烦躁的宝宝只有在爸爸怀里才安静下来。
senses.why: Fussy also describes a baby who will not settle, because restlessness is a fuss without words.
senses.whyCN: fussy 也形容安顿不下来的婴儿，因为这种烦躁就是一场没有言语的 fuss。

senses.title: Needing delicate handling, of a machine
senses.definition: of a machine or process, working well only under careful conditions and small adjustments
senses.definitionCN: 指机器或工序只有在小心条件和细微调节下才正常
senses.example: The fussy old printer jams whenever the paper is slightly damp.
senses.exampleCN: 那台娇气的老打印机，纸稍微有点潮就会卡纸。
senses.why: A machine that needs constant small adjustments behaves like a person who fusses, so the sense transfers to things.
senses.whyCN: 需要不停微调的机器，就像爱折腾的人，于是这层意思转到了物件上。

senses.title: Full of small troublesome details
senses.definition: of a task or procedure, made up of many small steps that demand care and patience
senses.definitionCN: 指任务或程序由许多需要耐心处理的小步骤组成
senses.example: Filing the receipts is a fussy job that nobody wants.
senses.exampleCN: 整理票据是件没人愿意做的琐碎活儿。
senses.why: A task full of tiny steps produces fuss, and anything that produces fuss is fussy to handle.
senses.whyCN: 满是细小步骤的任务会生出 fuss，凡是会生出 fuss 的东西，处理起来就繁琐。

intro.en: Fussy is built inside English from fuss plus the adjective suffix -y, and it dates from the late eighteenth century.
intro.cn: fussy 是英语内部由 fuss 加形容词后缀 -y 构成的，出现于十八世纪后期。

items.en: Fuss appears in English, probably as an echoic word, in the late eighteenth century.
items.cn: fuss 大约在十八世纪后期出现在英语中，很可能是拟声词。

items.en: The suffix -y turns a noun into an adjective meaning full of that thing.
items.cn: 后缀 -y 把名词变成形容词，表示「充满了这种东西」。

items.en: Fussy is recorded first for people who fuss, then for things crowded with small details.
items.cn: fussy 最早记录用来形容爱折腾的人，后来才形容堆满细碎细节的东西。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adjective extends to babies, machines and interior design.
items.cn: 二十世纪时，这个形容词扩展到婴儿、机器与室内装饰。

items.en: Fussily and fussiness complete the family, and fuss itself remains of uncertain origin.
items.cn: fussily 与 fussiness 补齐了这个词族，而 fuss 本身的来源仍不确定。

note.en: Fussy is the adjective of fuss, close in meaning to picky and finicky but wider in range.
note.cn: fussy 是 fuss 的形容词，与 picky、finicky 意义相近，但覆盖范围更宽。

entries.definition: unnecessary excitement or bustle about something small
entries.definitionCN: 为小事而生的多余激动或忙乱

entries.definition: in an overcareful, detail-obsessed way
the quality of being hard to please
choosing carefully and rejecting many things, especially food
paying too much attention to small details and difficult to satisfy
entries.definitionCN: 过分讲究细节的；难伺候的

entries.definition: demanding that things be done exactly as one likes

normalIntro.en: Fussy is fuss made into an adjective: a person or thing so full of fuss that nothing satisfies it.
normalIntro.cn: fussy 是把 fuss 变成了形容词：一个人或一件东西满是小题大做，怎么都不满意。

normal.en: Fussy is fuss plus -y, literally full of fuss.
normal.cn: fussy 是 fuss 加 -y，字面就是「满是 fuss」。

normal.en: A fussy eater rejects half the menu before ordering.
normal.cn: 「a fussy eater」还没点菜就先把半本菜单否掉。

normal.en: Fussy about something means holding very high standards for it.
normal.cn: 「fussy about」某件事，就是对它抱着极高的标准。

normal.en: A fussy design is crowded with frills and small ornaments.
normal.cn: 「a fussy design」就是堆满褶边和小饰物的设计。

normal.en: Compare picky: picky is informal and about choosing, while fussy also covers details and babies.
normal.cn: 对比 picky：picky 更口语，只管挑选；fussy 还覆盖细节和婴儿。

abstract.en: Picture a plate of peas sorted one by one, the rejected ones pushed to the rim.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘豆子被一颗颗分拣，不合心意的全推到盘子边缘。

abstract.en: Picture someone measuring a picture frame twice before hanging it.
abstract.cn: 想象有人挂画前把画框量了两遍。

abstract.en: Picture a dress carrying so many bows that the fabric disappears.
abstract.cn: 想象一条裙子缀满蝴蝶结，连布料都看不见了。

examples.en: The hotel staff were attentive without being fussy.
examples.cn: 酒店员工照顾得周到，却不过分殷勤。

examples.en: He is fussy about the temperature of his coffee.
examples.cn: 他对咖啡的温度很讲究。

examples.en: The fussy pattern on the curtains hurt my eyes.
examples.cn: 窗帘上花哨的图案看得我眼睛发疼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「发丝」——连一根发丝都要挑出来，可见有多挑剔；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 由英语 fuss（忙乱、大惊小怪）加形容词后缀 -y 构成，字面义「满是 fuss 的」，所以指爱挑剔、过分讲究、繁琐难弄；fuss 本身来源不确定，一般认为出自拟声。

sensesIntro.en: Fussy starts with the choosy eater, extends to over-exact standards and over-decorated objects, and ends with restless babies, delicate machines and detail-heavy tasks.
sensesIntro.cn: fussy 从挑食的人讲起，延伸到过分精确的标准与装饰过度的物件，最后落在烦躁的婴儿、娇气的机器和细节繁多的任务上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate of peas sorted one by one, the bad ones pushed aside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盘豆子被一颗颗挑拣，不合心意的都被拨到一边。

branches.en: The choosy eater is the everyday face of the word.
branches.cn: 挑食的人是这个词最日常的面孔。

branches.en: Exact standards for small details are the second step away from fuss.
branches.cn: 对小细节的精确标准，是离开 fuss 本义的第二步。

branches.en: Decoration piled on decoration is the design sense.
branches.cn: 一层压一层的装饰，是它的设计义项。

branches.en: A crying baby and a detail-heavy task both show fuss that will not settle.
branches.cn: 哭闹的婴儿与细节繁多的任务，都表现出安顿不下来的 fuss。

branches.en: A person fussy about standards and a machine needing small adjustments behave alike.
branches.cn: 对标准挑剔的人与需要细微调节的机器，行事方式如出一辙。

intro.en: Fussy is the adjective of fuss, and the suffixes -y, -ly and -ness hold the family together.
intro.cn: fussy 是 fuss 的形容词，-y、-ly 与 -ness 三个后缀把这个词族连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Fussy is built inside English on fuss, whose origin is uncertain, so no Latin relatives are listed.
latinIntro.cn: fussy 是英语内部以 fuss 为基础构成的，而 fuss 来源不确定，所以不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Fuss is the stem that fussy is built on.
items.exampleCN: fuss 是构成 fussy 的词干。

items.meaning: to complain or bustle about trifles
items.example: The verb fuss supplies the idea of restless activity.
items.exampleCN: 动词 fuss 提供了「停不下来的忙乱」这一层意思。

items.example: The suffix -y turns the noun into the adjective fussy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把这个名词变成形容词 fussy。

items.example: Fussy describes a person or thing full of fuss.
items.exampleCN: fussy 形容满是折腾的人或物。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb fussily.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 fussily。

items.example: Fussily says how the fussy person behaves.
items.exampleCN: fussily 说明爱挑剔的人怎样行事。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms the noun fussiness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成名词 fussiness。

items.meaning: the quality of being hard to please
items.example: Fussiness names the quality in the abstract.
items.exampleCN: fussiness 抽象地指这种性质。

items.meaning: a person who fusses about small things
items.example: Fussbudget is a close cousin of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: fussbudget 是这个形容词的近亲。

items.meaningCN: 过分挑剔的；过于繁复的
items.example: Overfussy adds the prefix over- to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: overfussy 给这个形容词加上前缀 over-。

definition_zh: 未来主义的；未来感的；极其现代化的；科幻式的
definition_en: looking like or relating to the imagined future, especially in design or technology
core_image: 一座银色建筑悬在半空，线条像飞船，门一开就滑出一道光带
scene: 展馆里那台银色机器没有按钮，只有一片浮在空中的光。The silver machine looked futuristic, with panels floating in the air instead of buttons.
sceneCN: 这里 futuristic 是「未来感的、科幻式的」（第 1 个义项：外形或技术让人想到想象中的未来）；句意：那台银色机器看起来像来自未来，面板浮在空中，而不是按钮。

pos.zh: 未来主义的；未来感的；极其现代化的；科幻式的

derivatives.zh: 由 future 加名词后缀 -ism 构成，义为「未来主义」，也指二十世纪初的意大利艺术流派
由 future 加 -ist 构成，义为「未来主义者；未来学家」
future 与 -ology 组合而成，义为「未来学」，研究未来趋势
由 futuristic 加 -ally 构成，义为「以未来主义的方式；带着未来感地」

senses.title: Looking like the imagined future
senses.definition: designed or built in a way that suggests the technology or style of the imagined future
senses.definitionCN: 设计或建造得让人想到想象中的未来技术与风格
senses.example: The lobby was lit by futuristic panels that changed colour.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅由会变色的未来感面板照亮。
senses.why: The adjective takes the Latin future participle futurus, so it points at what has not yet arrived and dresses objects as if they came from there.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词取自拉丁语将来分词 futurus，指向尚未到来的东西，并把物件打扮成好像来自那里。

senses.title: Relating to forecasting the future
senses.definition: connected with the study of future trends, scenarios, and long-range forecasts
senses.definitionCN: 与研究未来趋势、情景和长期预测的学问相关
senses.example: The report offers a futuristic view of transport in coastal cities.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告对沿海城市的交通提出了着眼未来的看法。
senses.why: Once the word means of the future, it can name any study or forecast that tries to describe it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「属于未来」，它就能指任何试图描述未来的研究或预测。

senses.title: Belonging to the Futurism movement
senses.definition: of or belonging to Futurism, the early twentieth-century art and literary movement that glorified speed and machines
senses.definitionCN: 属于未来主义的，即二十世纪初颂扬速度与机器的艺术与文学流派
senses.example: The gallery devoted a room to futuristic paintings of engines and crowds.
senses.exampleCN: 美术馆专门腾出一间展厅，陈列以引擎和人群为题材的未来主义绘画。
senses.why: The art movement Futurism was launched in 1909, and its name gave the adjective its first recorded use.
senses.whyCN: 未来主义流派于一九零九年发起，它的名字给了这个形容词最早的用法。

senses.title: Extremely modern, ahead of its time
senses.titleCN: 极其新潮的；超前于时代的
senses.definition: so modern in style or method that it seems to belong to a later period
senses.definitionCN: 在风格或方法上现代到仿佛属于更晚的时代
senses.example: For a machine built in the sixties, it still looks futuristic.
senses.exampleCN: 对一台六十年代造的机器来说，它看上去仍然超前。
senses.why: Anything that jumps ahead of its own period looks as if it had been borrowed from the future, so modern becomes futuristic.
senses.whyCN: 凡是跳出自己年代的东西，都像从未来借来的，于是「现代」就成了「未来感」。

senses.title: Visionary and far-sighted
senses.definition: of ideas or plans, concerned with the distant future rather than present needs
senses.definitionCN: 指想法或计划着眼于遥远的未来，而不是当下的需要
senses.example: Her futuristic plan for the harbour was dismissed as fantasy.
senses.exampleCN: 她那份着眼未来的港口方案被当成空想否决了。
senses.why: A plan can also be futuristic: it is drawn as if the far future were already the present.
senses.whyCN: 计划也可以是 futuristic：它画出来时，仿佛遥远的未来已经是现在。

senses.title: Science-fiction in style
senses.definition: of films, books, or games, set in an imagined high-technology future
senses.definitionCN: 指电影、书或游戏设定在想象的高科技未来
senses.example: The film mixes futuristic cities with very old machines.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影把科幻风格的城市和很旧的机器混在一起。
senses.why: Science fiction is the place where imagined futures are built, so the adjective naturally labels its style.
senses.whyCN: 科幻是想象未来被建造出来的地方，所以这个形容词自然用来标注它的风格。

intro.en: Futuristic joins the Latin future participle futurus, through English future, to the suffix -istic, and its first recorded use belongs to the art movement Futurism.
intro.cn: futuristic 由拉丁语将来分词 futurus 经英语 future 接上后缀 -istic 构成，最早的用法属于未来主义艺术流派。

items.en: Futurus is the future participle of esse, meaning about to be or going to be.
items.cn: futurus 是拉丁语动词 esse 的将来分词，意为「将要存在的」。

items.en: The suffix -isticus comes from Greek -istikos and passes into Latin adjectives.
items.cn: 后缀 -isticus 来自希腊语 -istikos，进入拉丁语形容词。

items.en: Marinetti launches Futurism, an art movement that celebrates speed, machines and the future.
items.cn: 马里内蒂发起未来主义，一个颂扬速度、机器与未来的艺术流派。

items.en: Futuristic is recorded in English for writing and painting that belong to that movement.
items.cn: 英语中的 futuristic 最早用来形容属于该流派的写作与绘画。

items.en: After the war the adjective moves to design, architecture and technology that looks ahead.
items.cn: 战后这个形容词转向着眼于未来的设计、建筑与技术。

items.en: Today it labels anything with a science-fiction look, from cars to kitchen appliances.
items.cn: 如今它标注一切带科幻外观的东西，从汽车到厨房电器。

note.en: Futuristic sits at the centre of the future word family, next to futurism and futurology, and near modern and cutting-edge.
note.cn: futuristic 位于 future 词族的中心，旁边是 futurism 与 futurology，并与 modern、cutting-edge 意义相近。

entries.definition: an early twentieth-century art movement, or any belief centred on the future
entries.definitionCN: 二十世纪初的艺术流派，也指任何以未来为中心的信念

entries.definition: a member of that movement, or a person who studies future trends
entries.definitionCN: 该流派的成员，或研究未来趋势的人

entries.definition: the study of probable future developments
entries.definitionCN: 未来学；对未来发展的研究

entries.definition: belonging to the present time or the recent past
entries.definitionCN: 现代的；属于当下或近代的

entries.definition: at the newest stage of development
having ideas about the future that seem imaginative rather than practical
entries.definitionCN: 有远见的；想法超前而不太实际的

normalIntro.en: Futuristic carries the future inside it, so any object that seems borrowed from tomorrow can wear the word.
normalIntro.cn: futuristic 里面就装着 future，任何像从明天借来的物件都能戴上这个词。

normal.en: Future plus -istic gives futuristic, an adjective meaning of the future.
normal.cn: future 加 -istic 就是 futuristic，一个意为「属于未来的」形容词。

normal.en: Futurism was an Italian art movement launched in 1909, and futuristic first described it.
normal.cn: 未来主义是一九零九年发起的意大利艺术流派，futuristic 最早就是形容它的。

normal.en: Futuristic design means curved panels and light instead of buttons and switches.
normal.cn: 「futuristic design」指弧面板与光，而不是按钮和开关。

normal.en: Futurology studies future trends, and a futuristic report does the same work in words.
normal.cn: futurology 研究未来趋势，而一份 futuristic 报告用文字做同样的工作。

normal.en: Compare modern: modern means of today, futuristic means of tomorrow.
normal.cn: 对比 modern：modern 属于今天，futuristic 属于明天。

abstract.en: Picture a silver tower whose floors float one above the other with no visible support.
abstract.cn: 想象一座银色高塔，楼层一层层悬着，看不见任何支撑。

abstract.en: Picture a car with no wheels, resting on a glow that lifts it off the road.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆没有轮子的车，靠一团光托离路面。

abstract.en: Picture a phone that is only a sheet of light lying on the table.
abstract.cn: 想象一部手机只是桌上一片发光的薄片。

examples.en: The new station has a futuristic roof of glass and steel.
examples.cn: 新车站有一片玻璃与钢构成的未来感屋顶。

examples.en: Designers in the sixties dreamed of futuristic kitchens.
examples.cn: 六十年代的设计师幻想过未来式的厨房。

examples.en: The film is set in a futuristic city above the clouds.
examples.cn: 这部电影的背景是云层之上的未来城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛特瑞斯提克」——念起来像科幻片里报出的机器编号，所以记「未来感」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 futurus（将要存在的，动词 esse 的将来分词）→ 英语 future（未来）+ 后缀 -istic → futuristic，字面义「属于未来的」；二十世纪初先指意大利未来主义流派，后来转指设计与技术的未来感。

sensesIntro.en: Futuristic starts as the adjective of an art movement, then widens to anything that looks like the imagined future, to forecasts, to what is ahead of its time, to far-sighted plans and to science fiction.
sensesIntro.cn: futuristic 起初是艺术流派的形容词，随后扩展到一切像想象中未来的东西，又延伸到预测、超前于时代的事物、着眼未来的方案以及科幻作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a silver building floating above the ground, its door opening in a band of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座悬在地面上的银色建筑，门一开就滑出一道光带。

branches.en: The core sense is an object that looks borrowed from the imagined future.
branches.cn: 核心义项是看起来从想象未来借来的物件。

branches.en: Forecasts and far-sighted plans both try to make the future present on paper.
branches.cn: 预测与着眼未来的方案，都是想把未来提前写在纸上。

branches.en: The art movement sense is the historical starting point of the word.
branches.cn: 艺术流派义项是这个词历史上的起点。

branches.en: Anything ahead of its time wears the same future look.
branches.cn: 任何超前于时代的东西都带着同样的未来外观。

branches.en: Science fiction is where imagined futures are built, so its style borrows the word.
branches.cn: 科幻是想象未来被建造的地方，所以它的风格借用了这个词。

intro.en: Futuristic is future plus -istic, and the family includes futurism, futurist, futurology and futurologist.
intro.cn: futuristic 是 future 加 -istic，同族词包括 futurism、futurist、futurology 与 futurologist。

latinIntro.en: Latin futurus, the future participle of esse, is the ultimate source of future, and -isticus supplies the suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 futurus 是 esse 的将来分词，也是 future 的最终来源，后缀则来自 -isticus。

items.meaning: about to be, going to be
items.meaningCN: 将要存在的；即将成为的
items.example: Futurus is the future participle of the verb to be.
items.exampleCN: futurus 是动词「存在」的将来分词。

items.meaning: the time that has not yet come
items.example: Future carries the participle into English as a noun.
items.exampleCN: future 把这个分词作为名词带进英语。

items.example: The suffix -istic builds adjectives from nouns.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -istic 从名词构成形容词。

items.meaning: of or like the imagined future
items.example: Futuristic joins future to the suffix -istic.
items.exampleCN: futuristic 把 future 接到后缀 -istic 上。

items.meaning: the art movement, or belief in the future
items.meaningCN: 未来主义；对未来中心的信念
items.example: The suffix -ism makes a movement out of future.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 用 future 造出一个流派名。

items.meaning: a member of the movement or a forecaster
items.example: The suffix -ist names a person connected with it.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 指与之相关的人。

items.example: Futurology joins future to the suffix -ology.
items.exampleCN: futurology 把 future 接到后缀 -ology 上。

items.meaning: a person who studies future trends
items.example: The suffix -ist turns futurology into a person.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 把 futurology 变成指人的词。

items.example: The suffix -ally forms the adverb futuristically.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ally 构成副词 futuristically。

items.example: Futuristically describes how something is designed.
items.exampleCN: futuristically 描述某物被设计的方式。

definition_zh: 小装置（总称）；精巧的小器具；小玩意儿
definition_en: small devices or tools considered as a group
core_image: 抽屉一拉开，满眼是带按钮和线的小玩意儿，多数只用过一次
scene: 厨房台面上堆着削皮器、计时器和一堆叫不出名字的小工具。The kitchen counter was crowded with gadgetry that nobody had used for years.
sceneCN: 这里 gadgetry 是「各种小装置的总称」（第 1 个义项：作为一类来看待的小器具）；句意：厨房台面上堆满了多年没人用过的小玩意儿。

pos.zh: 小装置（总称）；精巧的小器具；小玩意儿

derivatives.zh: gadgetry 的词干，义为「小装置；小玩意儿」，可数
由 gadget 加表人后缀 -eer 构成，义为「爱捣鼓小装置的人」
由 gadget 加 -y 构成，口语形容「小装置特别多的」

senses.title: A collection of small devices
senses.definition: small devices and tools spoken of together as one mass
senses.definitionCN: 把各种小装置和小工具作为一个整体来谈
senses.example: The shelf holds a tangle of gadgetry for opening jars.
senses.exampleCN: 架子上堆着一团用来开罐子的小器具。
senses.why: Gadgetry is a collective noun: the suffix -ry gathers many gadgets into one mass, much as cutlery gathers many knives.
senses.whyCN: gadgetry 是集合名词：后缀 -ry 把许多 gadget 收成一堆，就像 cutlery 把许多刀收成一套。

senses.title: The craft and industry of gadgets
senses.titleCN: 小器具技术；小装置产业
senses.definition: the design, production, or use of small devices as a field of activity
senses.definitionCN: 作为一项活动领域，指小装置的设计、生产或使用
senses.example: The fair is a showcase for consumer gadgetry.
senses.exampleCN: 这场博览会是消费类小装置的展示场。
senses.why: When a mass of gadgets becomes an activity, the word names the craft and industry that produce them.
senses.whyCN: 当一堆小装置变成一项活动时，这个词就指生产它们的手艺与产业。

senses.title: An excess of showy devices
senses.definition: devices regarded as unnecessary, gimmicky, or bought for show
senses.definitionCN: 被认为多余、花哨或只为摆样子而买的小装置
senses.example: The flat is impressive but full of pointless gadgetry.
senses.exampleCN: 这套公寓很气派，却塞满没用的小玩意儿。
senses.why: A collection can also be too much, so the same collective noun turns critical when devices are showy and useless.
senses.whyCN: 收藏也可能过头，于是这个集合名词在指花哨无用的装置时就带上了批评意味。

senses.title: Specialised kit for a trade or hobby
senses.titleCN: 某一行业的专用小器具
senses.definition: the small specialised tools that a profession or pastime depends on
senses.definitionCN: 某个行业或业余爱好所依赖的专用小工具
senses.example: A photographer carries gadgetry that fills two cases.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师带着的小器具能装满两个箱子。
senses.why: Any trade that relies on small tools builds its own gadgetry, so the word attaches to specialised kit.
senses.whyCN: 任何依赖小工具的行业都会攒出自己的 gadgetry，于是这个词也贴在专业装备上。

senses.title: Playthings for technology enthusiasts
senses.definition: devices bought mainly for the pleasure of owning and trying them
senses.definitionCN: 主要为拥有和试玩的乐趣而买下的装置
senses.example: His desk is covered in gadgetry he reviews on video.
senses.exampleCN: 他的桌上堆满他在视频里测评的小玩意儿。
senses.why: Enthusiasts buy gadgets for the pleasure of them, and the mass noun then names their toys.
senses.whyCN: 爱好者买小装置是为了其中的乐趣，这个集合名词于是也指他们的玩具。

intro.en: Gadgetry is an English collective noun built on gadget with the suffix -ry, and the origin of gadget itself is uncertain.
intro.cn: gadgetry 是英语内部以 gadget 为基础加集合后缀 -ry 构成的，而 gadget 本身的来源并不确定。

items.en: Gadget appears in English in the mid nineteenth century, first in nautical and mechanical talk.
items.cn: gadget 在十九世纪中期出现在英语里，最早见于航海与机械方面的谈论。

items.en: No source for gadget is agreed; dictionaries call its origin uncertain.
items.cn: gadget 的来源没有定论，各家词典都称其来源不确定。

items.en: One repeated suggestion links it to French gâchette, a small piece of a lock.
items.cn: 一种反复出现的猜测把它和法语 gâchette（锁具上的小零件）联系起来。

items.en: The suffix -ry, from French -erie, turns a countable noun into a collective one.
items.cn: 后缀 -ry 来自法语 -erie，把可数名词变成集合名词。

items.en: Gadgetry is recorded for the whole class of small devices, often with a critical tone.
items.cn: gadgetry 被用来指整个小装置类别，常带一点批评口吻。

note.en: Gadgetry is the collective of gadget, close to device and apparatus but always plural in feel.
note.cn: gadgetry 是 gadget 的集合形式，与 device、apparatus 意义相近，但总带「一群」的意味。

entries.definition: a small useful device, often clever but not essential
entries.definitionCN: 小巧有用的装置，常指巧妙但并非必需的东西

entries.definition: a person who is fond of gadgets
full of gadgets, in an informal style
entries.definitionCN: 小装置特别多的，口语用法

entries.definition: a piece of equipment made for a particular purpose
entries.definitionCN: 为特定用途制造的装置

entries.definition: a set of equipment used for a particular activity
entries.definitionCN: 为某项活动配备的一整套器材

entries.definition: a strange or complicated machine or device
entries.definitionCN: 古怪或复杂得有些可笑的装置

normalIntro.en: Gadgetry takes one gadget and adds the collective suffix, so the word always means a crowd of small devices.
normalIntro.cn: gadgetry 取一个 gadget 加上集合后缀，所以这个词永远指一大群小装置。

normal.en: Gadgetry is gadget plus -ry, and -ry makes a collective noun.
normal.cn: gadgetry 是 gadget 加 -ry，而 -ry 造出集合名词。

normal.en: The origin of gadget is uncertain, and French gâchette is only a suggestion.
normal.cn: gadget 的来源不确定，法语 gâchette 只是其中一种猜测。

normal.en: Electronic gadgetry now fills modern kitchens and office desks.
normal.cn: 「electronic gadgetry」如今塞满现代厨房和办公桌。

normal.en: Gadgeteer names the person who loves gadgetry.
normal.cn: gadgeteer 指的就是爱玩 gadgetry 的人。

normal.en: Compare device: a device is one thing, gadgetry is the whole class of small things.
normal.cn: 对比 device：device 是一件事物，gadgetry 是一整类小东西。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer pulled open, packed with chargers and tools used once.
abstract.cn: 想象拉开一只抽屉，里面塞满只用过一次的充电器和工具。

abstract.en: Picture a counter where every appliance has its own cable.
abstract.cn: 想象一个台面，每件电器都拖着各自的线。

abstract.en: Picture a shop window blinking with a hundred small screens.
abstract.cn: 想象橱窗里上百块小屏幕一起闪动。

examples.en: The garage is full of gadgetry he never uses.
examples.cn: 车库里塞满了他从没用过的小装置。

examples.en: Modern kitchen gadgetry can save time or simply fill drawers.
examples.cn: 现代厨房小器具能省时间，也可能只是塞满抽屉。

examples.en: She distrusts gadgetry and prefers a few simple tools.
examples.cn: 她不信这些小玩意儿，宁愿只用几件简单工具。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘎吉特瑞」——听着像抽屉里叮当乱响的一堆小玩意儿；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 gadget（十九世纪中期出现的小器具，来源不确定，一般认为可能与法语 gâchette「锁具上的小零件」有关）加集合后缀 -ry，构成「一类小装置的总称」。

sensesIntro.en: Gadgetry begins as a plain collective for small devices, then names the industry that makes them, the excess of showy ones, the kit of a trade, and finally the toys of enthusiasts.
sensesIntro.cn: gadgetry 起初只是小装置的普通集合名词，随后指制造它们的产业、花哨过头的玩意儿、某一行业的专用装备，最后指爱好者手里的玩具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open drawer packed with small devices used once and forgotten.
core.cn: 核心意象：拉开的抽屉塞满只用过一次就被遗忘的小装置。

branches.en: The core sense gathers many small devices into one word.
branches.cn: 核心义项把许多小装置收进一个词里。

branches.en: The industry sense turns that collection into a field of work.
branches.cn: 产业义项把这堆东西变成一项工作领域。

branches.en: The critical sense says the collection has grown too large and too showy.
branches.cn: 批评义项是说这堆东西已经太多、太花哨。

branches.en: Specialised kit is gadgetry narrowed to one trade or hobby.
branches.cn: 专用装备义项是把 gadgetry 缩小到一个行业或爱好。

branches.en: A collection of devices and a pile of toys differ only in who is playing.
branches.cn: 一堆装置和一堆玩具的区别，只在于谁在玩它们。

intro.en: Gadgetry is one stem plus one collective suffix, and the family adds -eer and -y to the same gadget.
intro.cn: gadgetry 是一个词干加一个集合后缀，同族词则在同一个 gadget 上加了 -eer 与 -y。

latinIntro.en: Gadget has no traced Latin source; French gâchette is only one suggested link, so no Latin relatives are listed.
latinIntro.cn: gadget 没有可追溯的拉丁语源头，法语 gâchette 只是其中一种猜测，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Gadget is the countable stem of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: gadget 是整个词族中可数的词干。

items.meaningCN: 表示同类事物总称的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ry gathers gadgets into gadgetry.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ry 把一个个 gadget 收成 gadgetry。

items.example: Gadgetry is uncountable and takes a singular verb.
items.exampleCN: gadgetry 不可数，动词用单数。

items.example: The suffix -eer marks a person devoted to gadgets.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -eer 标出痴迷小装置的人。

items.example: The suffix -y makes an informal adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 造出一个口语形容词。

items.meaning: a small piece of a lock mechanism
items.example: French gâchette is one suggested origin of gadget.
items.exampleCN: 法语 gâchette 是 gadget 的一种可能来源。

items.example: Device is the neutral word for one item of gadgetry.
items.exampleCN: device 是中性的说法，指 gadgetry 中的一件。

items.example: Apparatus is a formal near meaning of the word.
items.exampleCN: apparatus 是这个词的正式近义词。

items.example: Contraption adds a smile that gadgetry often shares.
items.exampleCN: contraption 添上 gadgetry 常有的那点笑意。

items.meaningCN: 硬件；包括电子装置在内的实体设备
items.example: Hardware is the commercial cousin of gadgetry.
items.exampleCN: hardware 是 gadgetry 在商业语境里的表亲。

definition_zh: 英勇；勇敢行为；殷勤；侠义之举
definition_en: brave and noble behaviour, especially in battle, or the courteous attention once paid to women
core_image: 一位骑士在危难中挺身而出，随后又优雅地向身旁的人伸手
scene: 老兵胸前挂着一枚勋章，那是当年在战场上为他赢来的。The old soldier wore a medal that he had won for gallantry on the battlefield.
sceneCN: 这里 gallantry 是「英勇」（第 1 个义项：面对危险时的无畏表现）；句意：这位老兵佩戴着一枚勋章，那是他在战场上凭英勇赢得的。

pos.zh: 英勇；勇敢行为；殷勤；侠义之举

derivatives.zh: 由古法语 galant 借入的形容词，义为「英勇的；高尚的；殷勤的」
gallant 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「英勇地；殷勤地」

senses.title: Bravery in the face of danger
senses.definition: courageous and noble behaviour, especially in battle or another dangerous situation
senses.definitionCN: 勇敢而高尚的行为，尤指在战斗或其他危险处境中的表现
senses.example: He was decorated for his gallantry under fire.
senses.exampleCN: 他因在炮火下的英勇表现而受勋。
senses.why: The earliest English sense of the family was a showy, spirited bearing, and that spirit hardened into plain courage when danger came.
senses.whyCN: 这一词族最早的英语含义是张扬而有活力的气派，危险来临时这种气派便沉淀为纯粹的勇气。

senses.title: Courteous attention to women
senses.definition: polite and attentive behaviour towards women, in the manner of an old-fashioned gentleman
senses.definitionCN: 以老派绅士的方式对女性表现出的礼貌与体贴
senses.example: His old-fashioned gallantry embarrassed the younger guests.
senses.exampleCN: 他那老派的殷勤让年轻的客人们感到不自在。
senses.why: The French source word meant courtly and amorous, so the English noun also names the ritual courtesy of a gentleman.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源词带有宫廷与爱慕之意，因此这个英语名词也指绅士式的礼节性殷勤。

senses.title: A gallant deed
senses.definition: a single brave, generous, or noble act
senses.definitionCN: 一次勇敢、慷慨或高尚的举动
senses.example: Rescuing the children from the flood was an act of pure gallantry.
senses.exampleCN: 从洪水中救出孩子们是纯粹的侠义之举。
senses.why: A quality can be counted through the deeds that show it, so the abstract noun also names single acts.
senses.whyCN: 一种品质可以通过体现它的行为来计数，因此这个抽象名词也可以指单个的举动。

senses.title: Noble, spirited bearing
senses.definition: a proud and spirited manner or style that marks a person as noble-hearted
senses.definitionCN: 显出胸襟高尚的骄傲而有生气的举止或风度
senses.example: There was a reckless gallantry in the way he threw himself into the work.
senses.exampleCN: 他投身工作的方式里有一种不顾一切的豪侠气概。
senses.why: The older sense of outward show survives as the manner of a whole person rather than as one action.
senses.whyCN: 较早的「外在气派」之义残留下来，指一个人的整体风度，而不是某一次行动。

intro.en: Gallantry comes through French from a word for high spirits and courtly show, not from a Latin noun of courage.
intro.cn: gallantry 经由法语而来，源头表示「兴致高昂」与「宫廷式的排场」，并非拉丁语中表示勇气的名词。

items.en: Galer means to rejoice or make merry; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: galer 意为欢欣、作乐；它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The participle galant describes a lively, showy, courtly person.
items.cn: 分词 galant 形容活泼、爱炫耀、有宫廷气度的人。

items.en: Galanterie names courtly courtesy and elegant display.
items.cn: galanterie 指宫廷式的礼节与优雅的排场。

items.en: Gallantry enters English as a word for fine appearance and polite address.
items.cn: gallantry 进入英语时指华美的外表与彬彬有礼的谈吐。

items.en: The sense of courage in battle grows out of the idea of a spirited, noble bearing.
items.cn: 战斗中的勇气之义由「有气概、高尚的风度」这一观念生长出来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the courage sense and the courtly courtesy sense side by side.
items.cn: 现代英语让「英勇」与「宫廷式殷勤」两个义项并存。

note.en: Gallantry sits with gallant and gallantly in English, and near the words for courage and for courtesy.
note.cn: gallantry 在英语中与 gallant、gallantly 同族，并与表示勇气和礼节的词相邻。

entries.definition: brave, noble, or politely attentive
in a brave or courteous way
existing in large numbers or amounts
entries.definitionCN: 大量的；充沛的；只是拼写相近，词源不同（源自爱尔兰语）

entries.definition: courage in facing danger or pain
polite behaviour that shows respect for others
the knightly code of honour, courage, and courtesy

normalIntro.en: Gallantry carries two pictures in one word: the knight who charges forward and the knight who bows.
normalIntro.cn: gallantry 一个词里装着两幅画面：向前冲锋的骑士，和躬身行礼的骑士。

normal.en: Gallant is the adjective behind gallantry, and both come from French.
normal.cn: gallant 是 gallantry 背后的形容词，两者都来自法语。

normal.en: A gallantry award is a medal given for a brave action.
normal.cn: gallantry award 是授予英勇行为的勋章。

normal.en: To show gallantry is to act with a spirited, noble courage.
normal.cn: show gallantry 就是以有气概的高尚勇气行事。

normal.en: The plural gallantries names several brave or courteous acts.
normal.cn: 复数 gallantries 指若干英勇或殷勤的举动。

normal.en: Compare the adverb gallantly, which describes how such an act is done.
normal.cn: 对比副词 gallantly，它描述这样的举动是如何做出的。

abstract.en: Picture a knight stepping out of the line to shield a fallen comrade.
abstract.cn: 想象一位骑士走出队列，护住倒下的同伴。

abstract.en: Picture the same knight offering his arm to a lady at a doorway.
abstract.cn: 想象同一位骑士在门口伸手让女士先行。

abstract.en: Picture one deed of rescue being written down in a chronicle.
abstract.cn: 想象一次救援的举动被记入编年史。

examples.en: The firefighter was praised for his gallantry in the burning building.
examples.cn: 这名消防员因在燃烧的大楼里的英勇表现受到赞扬。

examples.en: Old-fashioned gallantry made him hold the door for everyone.
examples.cn: 老派的殷勤让他为每个人扶住门。

examples.en: The chronicle records the gallantries of the local knights.
examples.cn: 编年史记载了当地骑士们的侠义之举。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘎兰特里」——想象一位叫嘎兰的骑士在特里河边挺身救人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 galer（欢欣、作乐）→ galant（活泼、有气派）→ galanterie（宫廷礼节与排场）→ 英语 gallantry，核心义「有气派的勇敢与殷勤」。

sensesIntro.en: Gallantry starts from a spirited, showy bearing, then splits into courage in danger, courtly courtesy, single noble deeds, and the bearing itself.
sensesIntro.cn: gallantry 从「有气派的昂扬风度」出发，分出危险中的勇气、宫廷式殷勤、单次侠义之举以及风度本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a knight who steps forward in danger and then bows to the person beside him.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位骑士在危难中挺身而出，随后向身旁的人躬身行礼。

branches.en: Courage in danger is the sense most used today.
branches.cn: 危险中的勇气是今天最常用的义项。

branches.en: Courtly courtesy is the old gentlemanly sense.
branches.cn: 宫廷式殷勤是那个老派绅士的义项。

branches.en: A single brave act is the countable sense.
branches.cn: 单次英勇举动是可数的义项。

branches.en: The bearing itself is the quality sense.
branches.cn: 风度本身是品质层面的义项。

branches.en: Both the quality and the deed are called gallantry, which is why the word counts acts and qualities alike.
branches.cn: 品质与举动都被称作 gallantry，因此这个词既可数举动也可指品质。

intro.en: Gallantry is built from a French adjective and a French noun suffix, with English adverbs and nouns grown around it.
intro.cn: gallantry 由法语形容词与法语名词后缀构成，英语在其周围长出副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin source; its elements are Old French, so no Latin cognates are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，其构件来自古法语，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Galer gives the high-spirited core.
items.exampleCN: galer 提供「兴致高昂」的核心。

items.meaningCN: 活泼的；有气派的；宫廷式的
items.example: Galant is the adjective borrowed into English as gallant.
items.exampleCN: galant 是借入英语成为 gallant 的形容词。

items.example: Galanterie is the direct model for the English noun.
items.exampleCN: galanterie 是英语名词的直接范本。

items.meaning: noun-forming suffix of quality or place
items.meaningCN: 构成名词、表示性质或场所的后缀
items.example: The suffix -erie builds galanterie.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -erie 构成 galanterie。

items.meaning: noun-forming suffix of quality or practice
items.meaningCN: 构成名词、表示性质或行为方式的后缀
items.example: English reshapes the ending as -ry in gallantry.
items.exampleCN: 英语把词尾改写为 -ry，构成 gallantry。

items.example: Gallant keeps both the brave and the courteous senses.
items.exampleCN: gallant 保留英勇与殷勤两个含义。

items.example: Gallantly describes the manner of acting.
items.exampleCN: gallantly 描述行事的方式。

items.example: Gallantry names the quality and its acts.
items.exampleCN: gallantry 指这种品质及其举动。

items.example: Gallantries counts the deeds.
items.exampleCN: gallantries 用来计数这些举动。

definition_zh: 赌博；打赌；冒险；押上；赌局
definition_en: to risk money or something valuable on an uncertain result, or such a risky act
core_image: 一叠筹码被推过绿色桌面，推向还没有翻开的骰子
scene: 朋友劝他别再往牌桌上添钱，他还是把最后一点积蓄推了出去。He decided to gamble his savings on one last hand of cards.
sceneCN: 这里 gamble 是「赌博；押上」（第 1 个义项：用钱押在结果不确定的赌局上）；句意：他决定把积蓄押在最后一手牌上。

pos.zh: 赌博；打赌；冒险；押上
赌局；冒险之举

collocations.zh: 高风险的赌注；孤注一掷

derivatives.zh: gamble 加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「赌徒；以赌为生的人」
gamble 加 -ing 构成动名词，义为「赌博；赌钱活动」

senses.title: To bet money on an uncertain outcome
senses.definition: to risk money on the result of a game, race, or other uncertain event
senses.definitionCN: 在游戏、赛马或其他结果不确定的事件上押钱
senses.example: They gambled all night at the card table.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整夜在牌桌上赌博。
senses.why: The word grew out of the language of playing games, so the first sense is literally to play for money.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「玩游戏」的说法里长出来，所以第一个义项字面上就是「为钱而玩」。

senses.title: To act on a risky hope
senses.definition: to do something risky in the hope of a good result
senses.definitionCN: 为求好结果而做有风险的事
senses.example: The company gambled on a young designer for its winter collection.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把冬季系列押在一位年轻设计师身上，这是一次冒险。
senses.why: Once money is staked, any hopeful risk can be pictured as a bet.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有了押上的本钱，任何抱着希望的冒险都可以被想象成一次下注。

senses.title: To stake something valuable
senses.definition: to put something valuable at risk, often with the chance of losing it completely
senses.definitionCN: 把有价值的东西置于风险中，常常有彻底失去的可能
senses.example: He gambled his reputation on the promise and lost it.
senses.exampleCN: 他把自己的名声押在那个承诺上，结果失去了它。
senses.why: The betting image extends from coins to reputation, health, and trust.
senses.whyCN: 下注的意象从钱币延伸到名声、健康与信任。

senses.title: A risky undertaking
senses.definition: a risky action or enterprise whose result is uncertain
senses.definitionCN: 结果不确定的冒险行动或事业
senses.example: Buying the farm was a gamble that finally paid off.
senses.exampleCN: 买下农场是一次最终得到回报的冒险。
senses.why: English turns the verb into a countable noun for the whole risky enterprise.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个动词转为可数名词，用来指整个有风险的举动。

intro.en: Gamble belongs to the English game family; its exact path is uncertain, and it is often described as a back-formation from gambler.
intro.cn: gamble 属于英语中表示「游戏」的词族；确切来源不确定，通常被视为由 gambler 逆构而成。

items.en: Game and the older noun gamen mean play and merrymaking.
items.cn: game 与较早的名词 gamen 意为玩耍与作乐。

items.en: A verb gamelen, to play at games, is recorded and may lie behind the modern word.
items.cn: 曾出现动词 gamelen，意为玩游戏，现代这个词可能源于它。

items.en: Gambler appears first, and gamble is generally taken to be formed from it.
items.cn: gambler 先出现，一般认为 gamble 是由它逆构而成。

items.en: The noun sense of a risky business develops alongside the verb.
items.cn: 表示「有风险的事业」的名词义与动词一起发展出来。

items.en: Modern English uses gamble for any calculated risk, from markets to marriages.
items.cn: 现代英语用 gamble 指任何权衡过的冒险，从市场到婚姻。

note.en: Gamble is close to the game words it grew from and to the vocabulary of betting and risk.
note.cn: gamble 与它源出的「游戏」词族相近，也与下注和风险的词汇相邻。

entries.definition: a person who bets money on games of chance
the activity of betting money
to skip or jump about playfully
entries.definitionCN: 欢蹦乱跳；只是读音相近，词源不同（源自古法语）

entries.definition: to risk money on the result of an event
to stake money on an uncertain outcome
to take a risky position in the hope of profit

normalIntro.en: Gamble lives in a family of game words, and its risk sense grew from the picture of stakes pushed onto a table.
normalIntro.cn: gamble 属于「游戏」词族，它的风险义从桌上押注的画面生长出来。

normal.en: Gamble and game share a history of play.
normal.cn: gamble 与 game 共享一段「玩耍」的历史。

normal.en: A gambler is the person, gambling is the activity, and gamble is the act.
normal.cn: gambler 指人，gambling 指活动，gamble 指那一次行为。

normal.en: You gamble on a team, a price, or a plan.
normal.cn: 你可以对一支球队、一个价格或一个计划下注。

normal.en: Gamble away means to lose something by betting.
normal.cn: gamble away 指赌输、输光某物。

normal.en: Take a gamble is the everyday phrase for trying something risky.
normal.cn: take a gamble 是「冒险一试」的日常说法。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a stack of chips into the middle of the table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一叠筹码推到桌子中央。

abstract.en: Picture a manager signing a contract with fingers crossed behind his back.
abstract.cn: 想象一位经理签下合同，手指在背后交叉。

abstract.en: Picture a reputation placed on the table beside the coins.
abstract.cn: 想象名声和钱币一起被摆在桌面上。

examples.en: He gambled away his wages in a single evening.
examples.cn: 他一晚上就把工资赌光了。

examples.en: Investors gamble on young firms in the hope of quick growth.
examples.cn: 投资者押注年轻公司，希望它们快速成长。

examples.en: Moving abroad without a job was a gamble she does not regret.
examples.cn: 没有工作就搬到国外是一次她并不后悔的冒险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘎姆波」——想象骰子在桌面上嘎一声滚过，筹码全被推走；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 game／gamen（游戏、作乐）→ gamelen（玩游戏）→ 一般认为由 gambler 逆构出 gamble，核心义「押上本钱去玩一场结果未定的局」。

sensesIntro.en: Gamble moves from betting money, to any hopeful risk, to staking something precious, and finally to the risky enterprise itself.
sensesIntro.cn: gamble 从押钱赌博，走到任何抱着希望的冒险，再到押上珍贵之物，最后指有风险的举动本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of chips pushed into the middle of the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠筹码被推到桌子中央。

branches.en: Betting money is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 押钱赌博是字面义项。

branches.en: A hopeful risk is the extended sense.
branches.cn: 抱着希望的冒险是延伸义项。

branches.en: Staking something precious is the transitive sense.
branches.cn: 押上珍贵之物是及物义项。

branches.en: The risky enterprise is the noun sense.
branches.cn: 有风险的举动是名词义项。

branches.en: Both betting and hopeful risk involve a stake and an unknown result.
branches.cn: 下注与抱着希望的冒险都包含押上的本钱和未知的结果。

intro.en: Gamble is a native English word built on game, with agent and gerund forms in -er and -ing.
intro.cn: gamble 是由 game 发展而来的英语本族词，用 -er 与 -ing 构成施事名词与动名词。

latinIntro.en: Gamble has no Latin source; it belongs to the Germanic game family, so no Latin cognates are listed.
latinIntro.cn: gamble 没有拉丁语来源，属于日耳曼语系的「游戏」词族，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Game is the family word behind gamble.
items.exampleCN: game 是 gamble 背后的词族词。

items.example: Gamen is the older form of game.
items.exampleCN: gamen 是 game 的较早形式。

items.example: Gamelen may be the verb that became gamble.
items.exampleCN: gamelen 可能就是变成 gamble 的那个动词。

items.example: The suffix -er names the person.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 指出人。

items.example: Gamble is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: gamble 是基础动词。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms gambling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 gambling。

items.example: Gambling names the activity.
items.exampleCN: gambling 指这种活动。

items.meaningCN: 第三人称单数现在时形式
items.example: Gambles is the present form with -s.
items.exampleCN: gambles 是加 -s 的现在时形式。

items.example: The particle away adds the idea of loss.
items.exampleCN: 小品词 away 增添「失去」之意。

definition_zh: 喋喋不休的；话多的；冗长啰嗦的
definition_en: talking too much, especially about unimportant things, or wordy and loosely organised in speech or writing
core_image: 一只停不下来的小鸟站在枝头，从早到晚唧唧喳喳，没有一句要紧话
scene: 茶室里那位常客一坐下就滔滔不绝，从天气讲到邻居家的狗，谁也没机会插话。The garrulous old man talked about the weather and the dog next door until everyone else fell silent.
sceneCN: 这里 garrulous 是「喋喋不休的」（第 1 个义项：话多、爱说琐事）；句意：那位喋喋不休的老人一直讲天气和邻居家的狗，直到别人都沉默下来。

pos.zh: 喋喋不休的；话多的；冗长啰嗦的

derivatives.zh: garrulous 去掉形容词词尾再加 -ity 构成，义为「喋喋不休；饶舌的习性」
garrulous 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「喋喋不休地；啰嗦地」
garrulous 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「话多的性质；啰嗦」

senses.title: Talking too much
senses.definition: fond of talking a great deal, especially about trivial matters
senses.definitionCN: 喜欢大量地说话，尤其是谈论琐碎小事
senses.example: Our garrulous neighbour can keep a conversation going for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 我们那位话多的邻居能把一段谈话拖上好几个小时。
senses.why: Latin garrulus describes a chatterer, so the word begins as a label for the person who will not stop talking.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 garrulus 形容爱唧唧喳喳的人，所以这个词一开始就是给「停不下嘴」的人贴的标签。

senses.title: Wordy and rambling
senses.definition: long-winded and loosely organised in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在言语或文字中冗长且结构松散
senses.example: The report is garrulous and short on facts.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告冗长啰嗦，事实却很少。
senses.why: A person who talks too much produces a text that talks too much, so the label moves from the speaker to the style.
senses.whyCN: 话多的人写出的话也太多，于是这个标签从说话者移到了文风。

senses.title: Fond of friendly chatter
senses.definition: sociable and fond of casual conversation, used with a milder tone
senses.definitionCN: 爱好社交、喜欢随意闲聊，语气较为温和
senses.example: In a garrulous mood she told us every detail of the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 她兴致上来、话特别多，把旅行的每个细节都讲给我们听。
senses.why: The same willingness to talk can look like warmth rather than excess, which gives the milder sense.
senses.whyCN: 同一种爱说话的意愿也可以显得亲切而非过滥，这就给出了较温和的义项。

intro.en: Garrulous comes straight from Latin, where it named a chattering bird or person.
intro.cn: garrulous 直接来自拉丁语，原指唧唧喳喳的鸟或人。

items.en: Garrire means to chatter, prattle, or babble.
items.cn: garrire 意为唧唧喳喳、喋喋不休。

items.en: Garrulus is the adjective for a chatterer, applied to birds and to talkative people.
items.cn: garrulus 是形容「爱唧喳者」的形容词，用于鸟和话多的人。

items.en: Garrulitas names the habit of chattering.
items.cn: garrulitas 指喋喋不休的习性。

items.en: English borrows garrulous as a label for a person who talks too much.
items.cn: 英语借入 garrulous，用来指话太多的人。

items.en: Modern English extends it to wordy writing and to merely sociable talk.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到啰嗦的文字以及仅仅是爱社交的谈话。

note.en: Garrulous belongs with garrulity and garrulously, and near the everyday words for talkative.
note.cn: garrulous 与 garrulity、garrulously 同族，并与日常表示「话多」的词相邻。

entries.definition: the habit of talking too much
in a chattering, wordy way
the quality of being garrulous
fond of talking
very talkative
using more words than are needed

normalIntro.en: Garrulous is a Latin bird word: the chatter of a small bird became a label for a talkative person.
normalIntro.cn: garrulous 是一个拉丁语的「鸟」词：小鸟的唧喳声变成了话多之人的标签。

normal.en: Garrulous, garrulity, and garrulously share one Latin root.
normal.cn: garrulous、garrulity、garrulously 共享一个拉丁词根。

normal.en: A garrulous person talks easily and long.
normal.cn: garrulous 的人说起来轻松又漫长。

normal.en: Garrulous writing is wordy and loosely built.
normal.cn: garrulous 的文字冗长且结构松散。

normal.en: Compare talkative, which is neutral, with garrulous, which mildly criticises.
normal.cn: 对比 talkative 的中性与 garrulous 的略带批评。

normal.en: Grow garrulous describes someone warming to a subject.
normal.cn: grow garrulous 描述某人越说越起劲。

abstract.en: Picture a small bird on a branch that will not stop chirping.
abstract.cn: 想象枝头一只停不下来的小鸟。

abstract.en: Picture a letter that runs to ten pages to say one thing.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信写了十页只说了一件事。

abstract.en: Picture two neighbours chatting at a gate while dinner cools.
abstract.cn: 想象两个邻居在门口闲聊，饭菜都凉了。

examples.en: He became garrulous after dinner and told the same story twice.
examples.cn: 晚饭后他话多起来，把同一个故事讲了两遍。

examples.en: Her garrulous letters were full of small talk and no news.
examples.cn: 她那些啰嗦的信里全是闲话，没有一条消息。

examples.en: The garrulous host barely let his guests speak.
examples.cn: 这位喋喋不休的主人几乎不让客人开口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘎噜勒斯」——想象一只鸟嘎噜嘎噜叫个不停，主人插不上话；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 garrire（唧唧喳喳）→ garrulus（爱唧喳的）→ 英语 garrulous，核心义「像小鸟一样停不下嘴」。

sensesIntro.en: Garrulous first labels the person who talks too much, then the wordy style such talk produces, then the milder pleasure in chatting.
sensesIntro.cn: garrulous 先给话多的人贴标签，再指这种话多所产生的啰嗦文风，最后指较温和的爱闲聊。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small bird that chirps on and on from its branch.
core.cn: 核心意象：枝头一只唧唧喳喳叫个不停的小鸟。

branches.en: The talkative person is the first sense.
branches.cn: 话多的人是第一个义项。

branches.en: Wordy style is the written extension.
branches.cn: 啰嗦文风是书面延伸义项。

branches.en: Friendly chatter is the milder social sense.
branches.cn: 友好闲聊是较温和的社交义项。

branches.en: Both senses describe someone who enjoys talking, differing only in tone.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述爱说话的人，只是语气不同。

branches.en: Endless talk and endless prose come from the same habit.
branches.cn: 说不完的话与写不完的句子出自同一种习性。

intro.en: Garrulous is built from a Latin verb and adjective, with English nouns and an adverb grown from it.
intro.cn: garrulous 由拉丁语动词与形容词构成，英语在其上长出名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin garrire means to chatter, and garrulus is the chattering adjective behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 garrire 意为唧唧喳喳，garrulus 是英语词背后的「爱唧喳」形容词。

items.example: Garrire is the sound at the centre of the word.
items.exampleCN: garrire 是这个词中心的声音。

items.example: Garrulus is the direct source of garrulous.
items.exampleCN: garrulus 是 garrulous 的直接来源。

items.example: Garrulitas names the habit.
items.exampleCN: garrulitas 指这种习性。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous turns garrulus into an English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 把 garrulus 变成英语形容词。

items.example: Garrulous keeps the Latin meaning.
items.exampleCN: garrulous 保留拉丁语含义。

items.example: The noun ending -ity replaces the Latin ending.
items.exampleCN: 名词词尾 -ity 替换了拉丁语词尾。

items.example: The adverb adds -ly to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 副词在形容词后加 -ly。

items.example: The suffix -ness names the quality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 指这种性质。

definition_zh: 汽油；(炼油中的)汽油馏分
definition_en: a light liquid fuel refined from petroleum and burned in engines
core_image: 一只油枪插进汽车油箱，微黄的液体带着刺鼻气味流进去
scene: 车子在高速路边熄了火，司机提着油桶走回加油站。The driver walked back to the station with a can of gasoline because the car had stopped on the highway.
sceneCN: 这里 gasoline 是「汽油」（第 1 个义项：用作内燃机燃料的轻质油品）；句意：车子在高速路上熄了火，司机提着一桶汽油走回加油站。

pos.zh: 汽油；汽油馏分

derivatives.zh: gasoline 的异体拼写，多见于早期文本与部分英式材料，义同「汽油」
gasoline 与过去分词 powered 构成的复合形容词，义为「汽油驱动的」
gasoline 与 alcohol 的缩合词，义为「汽油酒精混合燃料」

senses.title: Fuel for engines
senses.definition: a volatile liquid fuel refined from petroleum and burned in engines
senses.definitionCN: 由石油炼制的挥发性液体燃料，在内燃机中燃烧
senses.example: The tank holds forty litres of gasoline.
senses.exampleCN: 这个油箱能装四十升汽油。
senses.why: The word was coined for a petroleum fraction, and its everyday life is as the fuel pumped into vehicles.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一种石油馏分，它在日常生活中就是加进车辆的燃料。

senses.title: A petroleum distillate
senses.definition: the light petroleum fraction that boils within a low temperature range and serves as fuel or feedstock
senses.definitionCN: 沸点较低的轻质石油馏分，用作燃料或化工原料
senses.example: Refineries separate gasoline from heavier fractions by boiling point.
senses.exampleCN: 炼油厂按沸点把汽油馏分与较重的馏分分开。
senses.why: Chemical naming treats gasoline as one cut of the distillation, a substance rather than a product at the pump.
senses.whyCN: 化学命名把汽油看作分馏中的一段馏分，是一种物质，而不是加油机里的商品。

senses.title: Aviation-grade gasoline
senses.definition: a specially blended high-octane gasoline used in piston aircraft engines
senses.definitionCN: 用于活塞式航空发动机的、特殊调配的高辛烷值汽油
senses.example: The airfield stores aviation gasoline in sealed drums.
senses.exampleCN: 机场把航空汽油储存在密封的油桶里。
senses.why: Different engines need different blends, so the same word carries a grade label for aircraft.
senses.whyCN: 不同的发动机需要不同的调配，于是同一个词带上了供飞机使用的等级标签。

intro.en: Gasoline is a nineteenth-century chemical coinage, built on gas with the suffixes of the laboratory rather than on an old root.
intro.cn: gasoline 是十九世纪的化学造词，在 gas 之上加了实验室式的后缀，而不是从古老词根长成。

items.en: The Greek word khaos, meaning chaos or empty space, lies behind the later word gas.
items.cn: 希腊语 khaos 意为混沌、虚空，是后来 gas 一词的来源。

items.en: The chemist Van Helmont coins gas on the model of Greek khaos.
items.cn: 化学家范海尔蒙特仿希腊语 khaos 造出 gas 一词。

items.en: Gas takes the suffixes -ol and -ine to name a light petroleum liquid.
items.cn: gas 加上后缀 -ol 与 -ine，用来命名一种轻质石油液体。

items.en: Gasoline becomes the standard American word for motor fuel.
items.cn: gasoline 成为美式英语中表示车用燃料的标准词。

items.en: Modern English keeps gasoline for the fuel and petrol for the British equivalent.
items.cn: 现代英语用 gasoline 指这种燃料，英式则用 petrol。

note.en: Gasoline is close to its chemical building blocks and to the other names for fuel at the pump.
note.cn: gasoline 与其化学构件相近，也与加油机旁的其他燃料名称相邻。

entries.definition: an older variant spelling of the same fuel
entries.definitionCN: 同一燃料的较早异体拼写

entries.definition: the short everyday word for gasoline in American speech
entries.definitionCN: 美式口语中对汽油的简称

entries.definition: driven by a gasoline engine
entries.definitionCN: 汽油驱动的；由汽油发动机带动的

entries.definition: the British word for the same motor fuel
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语中同义的「汽油」

entries.definition: a heavier fuel used in compression-ignition engines
entries.definitionCN: 柴油；用于压燃式发动机的较重燃料

entries.definition: any material burned to produce heat or power
entries.definitionCN: 燃料；燃烧以产生热量或动力的物质

normalIntro.en: Gasoline is a laboratory name: gas plus two chemical suffixes, shortened to gas in daily speech.
normalIntro.cn: gasoline 是一个实验室式的名字：gas 加两个化学后缀，日常口语里又缩成 gas。

normal.en: Gasoline joins gas with the suffixes -ol and -ine.
normal.cn: gasoline 由 gas 加 -ol 与 -ine 构成。

normal.en: American drivers buy gasoline, while British drivers buy petrol.
normal.cn: 美国司机买 gasoline，英国司机买 petrol。

normal.en: Gas is the short form heard at American filling stations.
normal.cn: gas 是美国加油站里听到的简称。

normal.en: A gasoline engine burns the fuel inside its cylinders.
normal.cn: gasoline engine 在汽缸内燃烧燃料。

normal.en: To run out of gasoline leaves a car stranded.
normal.cn: run out of gasoline 会让车子抛锚。

abstract.en: Picture a nozzle clicking into a tank and the meter starting to run.
abstract.cn: 想象油枪卡进油箱，计量表开始跳字。

abstract.en: Picture a refinery tower splitting crude oil into floors of vapour.
abstract.cn: 想象炼油塔把原油按蒸气分到不同层。

abstract.en: Picture a small aircraft being fuelled from a sealed drum.
abstract.cn: 想象一架小飞机从密封油桶加油。

examples.en: Gasoline costs more in the city than in the countryside.
examples.cn: 城里的汽油比乡下贵。

examples.en: The generator needs a litre of gasoline to start.
examples.cn: 发电机需要一升汽油才能启动。

examples.en: Refiners blend gasolines for different engines and seasons.
examples.cn: 炼油厂为不同发动机和季节调配不同的汽油。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘎斯林」——想象汽油像嘎斯一声点着的蓝火苗；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 khaos（混沌）→ 荷兰语化学家造 gas → 英语 gas 加后缀 -ol 与 -ine → gasoline，核心义「从石油中炼出的轻质燃料」。

sensesIntro.en: Gasoline names one petroleum fraction, which becomes the everyday motor fuel, a refinery cut, and an aviation grade.
sensesIntro.cn: gasoline 指一种石油馏分，它既是日常车用燃料，也是炼油厂的一段馏分，又是航空用的等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nozzle locked into a fuel tank while the meter counts litres.
core.cn: 核心意象：油枪卡进油箱，计量表在数升数。

branches.en: Motor fuel is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 车用燃料是日常义项。

branches.en: The refinery fraction is the technical sense.
branches.cn: 炼油馏分是技术义项。

branches.en: The aviation grade is the specialised sense.
branches.cn: 航空等级是专门义项。

branches.en: The fuel at the pump is one cut of the distillation.
branches.cn: 加油机里的燃料就是分馏出来的一段。

branches.en: Both car fuel and aircraft fuel are blended gasoline grades.
branches.cn: 车用燃料与航空燃料都是调配过的汽油等级。

intro.en: Gasoline is assembled from a Greek-derived gas and two chemical suffixes, with compounds grown from it.
intro.cn: gasoline 由源自希腊语的 gas 与两个化学后缀组成，并由此长出复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source word here: gas goes back to Greek, and the suffixes belong to chemical naming.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语来源词：gas 追溯到希腊语，后缀属于化学命名体系。

items.example: Khaos is the Greek source behind gas.
items.exampleCN: khaos 是 gas 背后的希腊语来源。

items.example: Gas is coined from Greek khaos in the seventeenth century.
items.exampleCN: gas 于十七世纪仿希腊语 khaos 造出。

definition_zh: 美食学；烹饪艺术；饮食文化
definition_en: the art and science of cooking and eating well, or the food culture of a place
core_image: 一张摆满精致菜肴的长桌，旁边有人举杯讨论火候与产地
scene: 旅行作家在集市上尝了三种奶酪，回去后写了一整章谈当地饮食的门道。The travel writer tasted three cheeses at the market and later wrote a chapter on the gastronomy of the region.
sceneCN: 这里 gastronomy 是「饮食文化；烹饪艺术」（第 3 个义项：一个地方的饮食门道与风格）；句意：这位旅行作家在集市上尝了三种奶酪，后来写了一章讨论该地区的饮食文化。

pos.zh: 美食学；烹饪艺术；饮食文化

derivatives.zh: gastronomy 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「美食的；烹饪艺术的」
由 gastro-（胃）加 -nome（懂法则的人）构成，义为「美食家」
gastronomic 加 -ally 构成，义为「从美食角度；在饮食方面」

senses.title: The study of good eating
senses.definition: the study of cooking and of the pleasures and customs of eating
senses.definitionCN: 研究烹饪以及饮食之乐与饮食习俗的学问
senses.example: She studied gastronomy in Lyon before opening her restaurant.
senses.exampleCN: 她在里昂研习美食学，之后才开了自己的餐厅。
senses.why: The Greek compound means the law of the stomach, so the word begins as a body of knowledge about eating.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊语复合词意为「胃的法则」，所以这个词起初是一套关于饮食的学问。

senses.title: Fine cooking as a craft
senses.definition: the craft and artistry of preparing fine food
senses.definitionCN: 制作精致食物的手艺与艺术
senses.example: The chef treats gastronomy as a form of design.
senses.exampleCN: 这位主厨把烹饪艺术当作一种设计。
senses.why: Knowledge of eating turns into practice at the stove, so the word also names the craft of the kitchen.
senses.whyCN: 关于饮食的学问在灶台前变成实践，因此这个词也指厨房里的手艺。

senses.title: The food culture of a place
senses.definition: the characteristic cooking and eating habits of a region or group
senses.definitionCN: 某地区或群体特有的烹饪与饮食习惯
senses.example: The guide explains the gastronomy of the coast in a few pages.
senses.exampleCN: 这本指南用几页篇幅介绍了沿海的饮食文化。
senses.why: A region cooks and eats in its own way, so the learned word comes to mean the food culture of a place.
senses.whyCN: 一个地区有自己的烹饪与吃法，于是这个学术性的词也用来指一个地方的饮食文化。

intro.en: Gastronomy is a Greek compound stitched together from the words for stomach and for law, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: gastronomy 是一个希腊语复合词，由「胃」与「法则」两个词拼合，再经法语进入英语。

items.en: Gaster means stomach or belly.
items.cn: gaster 意为胃、腹部。

items.en: Nomos means law, rule, or custom.
items.cn: nomos 意为法则、规矩或习俗。

items.en: Gastronomia names the rules of the belly, a phrase used in classical writings on food.
items.cn: gastronomia 意为「胃的法则」，古典饮食著述中用过这一说法。

items.en: Gastronomie is coined in French in the early nineteenth century as a name for the art of eating well.
items.cn: gastronomie 于十九世纪初在法语中被造出，用来指「吃得好」的艺术。

items.en: English borrows gastronomy and applies it to cooking, dining, and regional food culture.
items.cn: 英语借入 gastronomy，用于烹饪、宴飨与地方饮食文化。

items.en: Modern gastronomy covers scientific cooking, restaurant craft, and food writing.
items.cn: 现代 gastronomy 涵盖科学烹饪、餐厅手艺与饮食写作。

note.en: Gastronomy is built from Greek roots and sits near gastronomic and gastronome, and beside the everyday words for food and cooking.
note.cn: gastronomy 由希腊词根构成，与 gastronomic、gastronome 同族，并与表示食物与烹饪的日常词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Gastronomy joins the Greek words for stomach and law: the rules of the belly turned into the art of eating well.
normalIntro.cn: gastronomy 把希腊语中「胃」与「法则」两个词接在一起：胃的规矩变成了吃得好的艺术。

normal.en: Gaster gives the gastro- element in gastronomy, gastritis, and gastronomic.
normal.cn: gaster 提供 gastronomy、gastritis、gastronomic 中的 gastro- 成分。

normal.en: Nomos means law, so gastronomy is literally a law of the stomach.
normal.cn: nomos 意为法则，所以 gastronomy 字面上就是「胃的法则」。

normal.en: A gastronome is a person devoted to fine food.
normal.cn: gastronome 是痴迷精致食物的人。

normal.en: Gastronomic describes anything that has to do with fine eating.
normal.cn: gastronomic 描述与精致饮食有关的一切。

normal.en: Regional gastronomy means the food culture of a place.
normal.cn: regional gastronomy 指一个地方的饮食文化。

abstract.cn: 想象一位学者在滚沸的锅旁做笔记。

abstract.en: Picture a chef measuring spice with the calm of a chemist.
abstract.cn: 想象一位厨师像化学家一样从容地量取香料。

abstract.cn: 想象一个集市摊位，全城的人都在争论奶酪。

examples.cn: 他写了一本关于地中海沿岸饮食文化的书。

examples.en: The festival celebrates both gastronomy and traditional music.
examples.cn: 这个节日既庆祝美食文化，也庆祝传统音乐。

examples.en: Modern gastronomy uses tools borrowed from the laboratory.
examples.cn: 现代烹饪艺术使用从实验室借来的工具。

root: 希腊语 gastēr（胃）+ nomos（法则、习俗）→ gastronomia（胃的法则）→ 法语 gastronomie → 英语 gastronomy，核心义「关于吃喝的学问与讲究」。

sensesIntro.en: Gastronomy begins as a name for the rules of eating well, then covers the craft of fine cooking and the food culture of a place.
sensesIntro.cn: gastronomy 起初指「吃得好的规矩」，随后涵盖精致烹饪的手艺与一个地方的饮食文化。

core.cn: 核心意象：一张摆满精心制作菜肴的长桌，有人在讨论它们的来历。

branches.en: The study of eating is the learned sense.
branches.cn: 关于饮食的学问是学术义项。

branches.en: Fine cooking is the craft sense.
branches.cn: 精致烹饪是手艺义项。

branches.en: Regional food culture is the social sense.
branches.cn: 地方饮食文化是社会义项。

branches.en: Study and craft meet in professional food writing.
branches.cn: 学问与手艺在专业的饮食写作中相遇。

branches.en: Cooking technique and local custom together make a cuisine.
branches.cn: 烹饪技术与地方习俗合起来构成一种菜系。

intro.en: Gastronomy joins two Greek roots, and English built gastronomic, gastronome, and gastronomically on it.
intro.cn: gastronomy 接合两个希腊词根，英语在其上构成 gastronomic、gastronome 与 gastronomically。

latinIntro.en: The elements are Greek rather than Latin, so no Latin cognates are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 其构件属于希腊语而非拉丁语，因此这里不列拉丁同源词。
